target.title: fix(e2e): keep phase log tails UTF-8 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`PhaseRunner` (`scripts/e2e/parallels/phase-runner.ts`) keeps a bounded in-memory log tail per phase (`appendTextTail`) and writes that tail to stderr when a phase fails. The bound is applied as a raw byte cut — `Buffer.from(combined).subarray(-tailBytes).toString("utf8")` — so when the retained window starts in the middle of a multi-byte UTF-8 character (emoji/CJK in test output), the diagnostics tail begins with U+FFFD replacement characters.

This is the same bug family as merged #109669 (`scripts/e2e/lib/text-file-utils.mjs`) and open sibling #109670 (`scripts/e2e/parallels/host-server.ts`); `phase-runner.ts` is the remaining byte-based tail decoder in the parallels harness. The three PRs touch separate files and are not stacked; any order merges cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

#109669 introduced `decodeUtf8Tail`, which drops leading UTF-8 continuation bytes before decoding a truncated window. This PR exports that helper and reuses it in `appendTextTail`, so the byte cap stays unchanged while the emitted tail always starts on a character boundary. The change is three lines in prod code plus a focused regression test.

Root cause on `main` (`scripts/e2e/parallels/phase-runner.ts:18`): the byte cut from `subarray(-tailBytes)` can start on a UTF-8 continuation byte, and `toString("utf8")` replaces each orphaned continuation byte with U+FFFD.

Deliberately out of scope: `scripts/e2e/parallels/filesystem.ts` has a similar byte-window read, but its only consumer is a regex scan (`extractLastOpenClawVersionFromLog`) whose ASCII pattern cannot straddle a character boundary, so a partial leading character there has no observable effect.

## User Impact

Maintainers reading failed E2E phase output get a clean log tail instead of leading mojibake whenever multibyte text (emoji in test names/output, CJK) crosses the 512 KiB tail cutoff.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof against the production `PhaseRunner` on `main` (driver: construct with a 128-byte cap, `append()` 134 bytes containing an emoji positioned so the byte window starts one byte into it, fail the phase, capture stderr):

Before (origin/main):

```
[phase log tail truncated to last 128 bytes]
���yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy
contains U+FFFD replacement char: true
```

After (this branch):

```
[phase log tail truncated to last 128 bytes]
yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy
contains U+FFFD replacement char: false
```

Regression coverage: `test/scripts/parallels-phase-runner.test.ts` drives the real class through a failing phase and asserts the stderr tail (1) contains no U+FFFD when the byte cut splits a character, (2) keeps the full emoji tail when the cut lands on a character boundary, (3) leaves short logs untruncated.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/parallels-phase-runner.test.ts` — 3/3 pass on this branch; the split-character test fails on unpatched `phase-runner.ts` (control-red verified by reverting the prod file to `origin/main`).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/e2e-text-file-utils.test.ts` — pass (sibling helper tests unaffected by the new export).
- `oxfmt --check` on all touched files — clean; `oxlint` on touched files — 0 findings; `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.scripts.json` — no errors in touched files (pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors come from a stale local `ipaddr.js@1.9.1`, unrelated).
- `git diff --check` — clean.

target.title: feat(onboard): browser-first guided handoff (draft — held on fresh-gateway auth)
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

Phase 3 of the custodian onboarding redesign: after guided onboarding verifies a
model and applies setup, hand the "hatch" to the browser dashboard instead of the
terminal TUI, so non-technical users land in the graphical Control UI.

**Status: DRAFT / held.** Live testing revealed the handoff's Control UI
presence read is rejected on fresh quickstart gateways (see Evidence); it works on
SecretRef-token local gateways. Because the failure path falls back cleanly to the
terminal hatch, nothing regresses, but the browser handoff should not be enabled by
default until the gateway token-resolution issue is fixed. Opening as a draft to
preserve the implementation and diagnosis for follow-up.

# Why This Change Was Made

- `src/commands/onboard-browser-handoff.ts`: GUI-vs-headless session detection
  (`SSH_CONNECTION`/`DISPLAY`), dashboard URL resolution (reusing the classic
  finalize helpers, not duplicating token/URL logic), a reachability preflight, and
  a wait loop that polls `system-presence` and completes only when a **new** Control
  UI client (baseline-diffed) connects. GUI opens the browser (60s wait); headless
  prints the URL + SSH hint (300s wait).
- Wired into the guided custodian flow (`onboard-guided.ts`) after recommendations,
  custodian-mode + darwin only, gated on gateway reachability, with a `--tui`
  escape hatch and graceful fallthrough to the terminal hatch.
- Presence is read as a CLI-mode loopback client (the trusted path every `openclaw`
  command uses) rather than a raw shared-auth Control UI client — this fixed the
  original "device identity required" rejection on SecretRef gateways.
- Skips the handoff when `gateway.controlUi.enabled` is false (avoids opening a dead
  URL and blocking for the full timeout).

# User Impact

No behavior change by default while held: onboarding still hatches in the terminal.
When enabled, GUI users get the dashboard opened automatically; headless/SSH users
get a copy-pasteable URL.

# Evidence

- 16 handoff unit tests + guided/custodian suites green; tsgo, oxlint, knip,
  import-cycles clean; my own autoreview clean.
- Live probe against a real SecretRef local gateway: `probeBrowserHatchGateway`
  returns `{ ok: true }` (previously `{ ok: false, "device identity required" }`).
- **Known blocker (why this is draft):** live headless onboarding against a fresh
  quickstart gateway fails the presence read with `unauthorized: gateway token
  mismatch (set gateway.remote.token to match gateway.auth.token)` — the token
  written to config resolves differently than the gateway's running token during
  in-process onboarding. The handoff falls back to the terminal hatch, so onboarding
  completes normally. Fix requires aligning the onboarding-time gateway token
  resolution; tracked in `docs/start/onboarding-redesign.md`.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): honor abortSignal in transient-HTTP retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The transient-HTTP retry in `handleAgentExecutionError` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-error-handler.ts:405-414`) waits out its backoff on a bare `setTimeout(resolve, TRANSIENT_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY_MS)` — 2 500 ms (`TRANSIENT_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 2_500`, line 60) — that never receives the turn's `AbortSignal`. When a reply turn is cancelled mid-backoff (user stop, session abort, gateway/channel teardown), the error handler stays parked for the full 2 500 ms, and — worse — it then returns `{ kind: "retry" }`, so the turn loop issues **another provider attempt** for a turn whose result will be discarded. Turn teardown is delayed for every auto-reply channel (telegram included) each time a transient HTTP provider error (5xx/timeout) races with a cancellation.

Sibling parity: the overload-retry branch ~30 lines above in the same function was made abort-aware by #109354 (merged 2026-07-16) — it computes `retryAbortSignal = turn.replyOperation?.abortSignal ?? turn.opts?.abortSignal` (line 275) and sleeps via `sleepWithAbort(retryDelayMs, retryAbortSignal)` inside a `try/catch` that maps the rejection through `resolveReplyOperationAbortAction` (lines 383-391). The transient-HTTP backoff was simply left behind.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the overload branch exactly. `sleepWithAbort` (`src/infra/backoff.ts`, re-exported from `packages/retry/src/index.ts:21`) and `resolveReplyOperationAbortAction` (line 130) are already imported/in scope in this file, and the same `turn.replyOperation?.abortSignal ?? turn.opts?.abortSignal` expression is what the caller already uses for `runAbortSignal` (`agent-runner-execution.ts:260`) and what the overload branch uses for its own retry sleep.

- Before: `await new Promise<void>((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, TRANSIENT_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY_MS); }); return { kind: "retry" };`
- After: compute `retryAbortSignal` (same expression as the overload branch), `await sleepWithAbort(TRANSIENT_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY_MS, retryAbortSignal)` inside the same `try/catch` → `resolveReplyOperationAbortAction(sleepError)` pattern (return the abort action when set, otherwise rethrow), then `return { kind: "retry" }` unchanged when not aborted.

No new config, no new constants, no new helpers, no behavior change when the signal is not aborted: the delay value, the single-retry budget, and the log line are untouched. Non-test LOC: `+10 / -3` on one file.

This follows the same bare-`setTimeout` → `sleepWithAbort` pattern as merged #108561 (discord gateway READY backoff) and #109604 (telegram startup probe retry).

## User Impact

Cancelling a reply turn (stop command, session reset, gateway shutdown, channel teardown) while a transient HTTP provider error retry is parked now unwinds the turn immediately with the abort lifecycle action (`NO_REPLY` for a user abort, restart copy for a restart abort) instead of waiting out the remaining backoff and firing one more doomed provider request.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — production handler, real `AbortController`, wall-clock

Uncommitted `scratchpad/proof-transient-retry-abort.mts` (not in this PR) calls the real exported `handleAgentExecutionError` with a transient-HTTP-shaped provider error (`521 <!DOCTYPE html>…Cloudflare…`), `consumeTransientHttpRetry: () => true`, a real `AbortController` wired as `turn.replyOperation.abortSignal`, and real wall-clock timers (no `vi.mock`, no fake timers). It lets the handler park in the backoff, fires `abort()` at ~100 ms, and measures abort-to-return.

**Before** (main @ `e01027dd28`, bare `setTimeout`):

```
Transient HTTP provider error before reply (521 <!DOCTYPE html>…). Retrying once in 2500ms.
{
  "abortToReturnMs": 2402.2,
  "totalHandlerMs": 2522.5,
  "resultKind": "retry"
}
```

Abort fired ~100 ms in; the handler still sat the full 2 500 ms backoff and then returned `retry` — i.e. the turn loop would run the provider again after cancellation.

**After** (this PR):

```
Transient HTTP provider error before reply (521 <!DOCTYPE html>…). Retrying once in 2500ms.
{
  "abortToReturnMs": 1.1,
  "totalHandlerMs": 119.2,
  "resultKind": "final",
  "payloadText": "NO_REPLY"
}
```

Same script, same timing: the abort interrupts the backoff in ~1 ms and the handler returns the user-abort lifecycle action.

Run with: `node --import tsx scratchpad/proof-transient-retry-abort.mts` (Node v24.15.0, Linux x86_64).

### Regression coverage

- New: `interrupts the transient HTTP retry backoff on abort` in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts` — drives `runAgentTurnWithFallback` with a transient failover error (`FailoverError` reason `timeout`, the same `isTransientHttp` branch; this test harness stubs message-based `isTransientHttpError` to `false`), aborts mid-backoff, and asserts the turn resolves to the user-abort final payload with no second provider attempt (`runEmbeddedAgentMock` called once).
- Existing: `retries once after transient 521 HTML failure and then succeeds` in `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` locks the non-abort behavior (waits the 2 500 ms, retries once, succeeds) — unchanged.

### Control-red verification

Reverting only the source hunk (keeping the new test) makes the new test hang indefinitely — the bare `setTimeout` parks the handler for the full backoff and nothing observes the abort; Vitest reported no output for 120 s and was terminated. Restoring the fix: pass. The wall-clock proof above shows the same contrast on the real handler (2 402 ms → 1.1 ms).

### Tests & checks

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts` — 66/66 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 75/75 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <both files>` — exit 0
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — exit 0
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` — exit 0
- `git diff --check` — clean

## Out of scope

The overload-retry branch (already abort-aware since #109354), the overload notice delivery timeout, and `TRANSIENT_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY_MS`'s value/retry budget are unchanged. Other bare sleeps elsewhere in the auto-reply runner were not touched.

## Risk

- User-visible behavior change? Yes — a cancelled turn now finishes promptly with the abort lifecycle action instead of sleeping out the transient retry backoff and issuing one more provider attempt. Happy-path (no abort) behavior is identical, locked by the existing 521 regression test.
- Config/env/migration change? No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-execution change? No.
- Highest-risk area: an abort that is neither a user abort nor a restart abort rethrows the sleep rejection exactly like the overload branch does (same `resolveReplyOperationAbortAction` fall-through), preserving existing semantics.

AI-assisted; reviewed before submission.

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout in `finally`.
- Added `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` exercising the real fetch path against a local HTTP server (not a fetch mock): stalled responses abort after the bound; normal 200 responses still resolve.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts`
- The stall cases use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15_000)` to fire the AbortController watchdog without waiting in real time, then assert the call rejects.

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
 - aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging  (pass)
 - aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip                  (pass)
 - still resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip                (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the server accepting the connection but never ending the response, both helpers reject (AbortError) after the 15s bound instead of remaining pending. With the server returning 200 JSON, both helpers resolve and return `{ ok: true, persisted: true }`, so ordinary profile operations are unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real Nostr relay was not executed (no relay credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix(compaction): keep mirror usage from poisoning truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running channel sessions could compact but fail to reclaim transcript history when a transcript-only `delivery-mirror` assistant row was the latest assistant entry. In that state, malformed mirror usage could poison `tokensBefore`, causing the compaction boundary to be dropped and the transcript to keep replaying old history.

Closes #100982

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction estimator now ignores OpenClaw transcript-only assistant artifacts for last-assistant usage sampling and reads token usage through finite, provider-shape-tolerant counters. Normal transcript replay stays strict to canonical compaction records with numeric `tokensBefore`.

For already-written compaction rows whose explicit `tokensBefore` value serialized as `null`, the Doctor transcript repair path now detects and rewrites the durable JSONL to canonical `tokensBefore: 0`. Omitted `tokensBefore` and other malformed values remain invalid instead of being accepted during replay.

## User Impact

Safeguard compaction can keep using the real model assistant usage instead of a channel mirror row, so sessions no longer get wedged by mirror usage producing invalid `tokensBefore` telemetry. Existing transcripts with explicit `tokensBefore: null` compaction rows can be repaired with `openclaw doctor --fix`; normal runtime reads then consume the rewritten canonical row.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts` -> 3 Vitest shards passed, 57 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` -> passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.ts src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts` -> all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check` -> no whitespace errors.
- Direct production-function proof is included below.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Compaction token estimation skips transcript-only `delivery-mirror` usage, keeps `tokensBefore` finite, and moves explicit-null compaction telemetry repair into Doctor before strict transcript replay.

**Environment tested:** Linux source checkout, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2.

**Steps run after the patch:** Ran the targeted regression tests, then ran a source-level proof script that imports the actual patched `prepareCompaction`, `detectSessionTranscriptHealthIssues`, `noteSessionTranscriptHealth`, and `readTranscriptFileState` functions. The proof uses a real assistant row followed by a `delivery-mirror` row carrying the OpenAI-style zero usage shape from the issue, plus JSONL files with explicit null and omitted compaction telemetry.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-transcripts.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts
node --import tsx --no-warnings /tmp/openclaw-100982-proof.mjs
```

**Evidence after fix:** Targeted tests:

```text
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 67.48s
```

Production source-level proof output:

```text
prepareCompaction: {
  "ok": true,
  "tokensBefore": 3034,
  "finite": true
}

doctorReplay: {
  "issuesBefore": [
    {
      "file": "null.jsonl",
      "nullCompactionCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "nullBeforeEntries": [
    "user-1",
    "user-2"
  ],
  "nullAfterCompaction": {
    "type": "compaction",
    "id": "compact-null",
    "parentId": "user-2",
    "timestamp": "2026-07-06T00:00:03Z",
    "summary": "summary",
    "firstKeptEntryId": "user-2",
    "tokensBefore": 0
  },
  "nullRawContainsCanonicalZero": true,
  "omittedBeforeEntries": [
    "user-1",
    "user-2"
  ],
  "omittedAfterEntries": [
    "user-1",
    "user-2"
  ],
  "omittedRawContainsTokensBefore": false
}
```

**Observed result:** The production compaction path returns finite telemetry from the real assistant row instead of the mirror row. Doctor detects and rewrites explicit `tokensBefore: null` rows to durable `tokensBefore: 0`, after which strict replay accepts the compaction boundary; omitted `tokensBefore` remains unrepaired and absent from strict replay.

**Not tested:** A live long-running Telegram or gateway safeguard compaction loop with real channel delivery was not run.

## Impact Assessment

- Scope: agent-core compaction token estimation, embedded transcript JSONL replay, and Doctor session transcript repair.
- Downstream: existing callers continue receiving numeric `tokensBefore`; transcript-only assistant rows are ignored only as usage sources, not removed from transcript state by this change.
- Edge cases: non-finite, negative, missing, `null`, OpenAI-style, and nested cache usage fields are covered by normalization, strict replay rejection, Doctor repair, or fallback estimation as appropriate.
- Hard-coded values: no runtime configuration defaults were added or changed.

target.title: fix(codex): timed-out native hooks exhaust memory
target.body:
Closes #109421

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex-backed agent jobs could leave timed-out native hook relay processes running on Linux, causing process fanout, multi-gigabyte memory growth, swap pressure, and eventual gateway or host OOM kills.

## Why This Change Was Made

POSIX native hook commands now replace Codex's timeout-owned shell with the relay process via `exec`. The internal `hooks relay` invocation also bypasses OpenClaw's packaged compile-cache, startup-environment, and general CLI respawn layers so the PID Codex terminates remains the relay PID throughout startup.

Windows behavior is unchanged because it needs a separate process-tree-aware termination or parent-watchdog design.

## User Impact

Linux operators running Codex native hooks should no longer accumulate relay children after hook timeouts. Timed-out hooks terminate the actual relay process instead of only an intermediate launcher, reducing task fanout and memory exhaustion during long agent jobs.

## Evidence

### Production incident and current-main reproduction

- Kernel OOM logs from the affected host recorded 19 `openclaw-hooks` processes using 3.84 GiB plus 30 launcher/startup `openclaw` processes using 2.56 GiB.
- The issue contains an independent current-main process-tree reproduction showing the timeout-owned shell dying while the launcher and detached relay survive.
- The same probe against this patch keeps one timeout-owned relay PID and leaves no survivor.

### Live Codex timeout on the final branch

A controlled run used OpenClaw's production `buildCodexNativeHookRelayConfig` through the real Codex 0.144.5 app-server `thread/start` path. Codex started the generated relay command, applied its own one-second hook timeout, emitted `hook/completed`, and left no recorded relay process alive.

Tested OpenClaw head: `a7e2531f0df471f7f79ab3ff09843df2b0953963`.

```text
codex_version=codex-cli 0.144.5
command_has_exec_prefix=true
generated_command=exec nice -n 10 .../node-with-tsx .../src/entry.ts hooks relay   --provider codex --relay-id codex-live-proof-missing   --event pre_tool_use --timeout 8000

before_codex_timeout
timeout_owned_relay_pid=1904306
recorded_relay_count=1

PID      PPID     PGID     SID      STAT  RSS_KiB  COMMAND
1904306  1903641  1903468  1903420  SNl   68420    node ... hooks relay ...

codex hook/completed
source=sessionFlags
event=preToolUse
executionMode=sync
status=failed
durationMs=1001
error="hook timed out after 1s"

after_codex_timeout
codex_exit_code=0
recorded_relay_count=1
surviving_relay_pids=(none)
relay_survived_timeout=false
```

The probe ran in a transient systemd service with `MemoryMax=2G`, `MemorySwapMax=1G`, `TasksMax=80`, and cleanup for every recorded PID.

### Codex dependency contract

Direct source inspection confirms the contract in both the incident version `rust-v0.144.3` and current OpenClaw dependency `rust-v0.144.5`; `command_runner.rs` is identical between those tags:

- The hook command is the directly spawned child with `kill_on_drop(true)`.
- The timeout wraps `child.wait_with_output()`.

Closes #109979

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp group messages from LID-based sender identities could log a successful configured ack reaction while the reaction did not render in the WhatsApp group thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

WhatsApp group reaction keys need the original sender participant. The ack and status reaction paths now resolve one shared participant value from the inbound sender identity, preferring the phone JID when present and falling back to the LID when that is the only available sender key.

## User Impact

WhatsApp group ack reactions should appear consistently for LID-only group senders, and temporary ack cleanup uses the same participant key so reactions do not get stranded.

## Summary

- Add a shared WhatsApp auto-reply reaction participant resolver that falls back from `sender.jid` to `sender.lid`.
- Use the shared participant resolution in both ack reactions and status reactions.
- Add regression coverage for JID preference, LID fallback, missing sender identity, ack send/remove, and status set/clear paths.

## Change Type

target.title: fix(e2e): keep telegram proof diagnostic tails Unicode safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Telegram user Crabbox proof script (`scripts/e2e/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts`) bounds several diagnostic tails that surface in failure output, and two cut shapes corrupt multibyte content (gateway logs for a Telegram proof are emoji/CJK-dense):

1. `readLogTail` (exported, used by `waitForLog` readiness errors) reads the last N **bytes** of a log file and decodes with `toString("utf8")` from the cut offset. A window starting inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character emits U+FFFD replacement characters at the start of the tail — the same bug merged #109669 fixed in `scripts/e2e/lib/text-file-utils.mjs`.
2. The rolling output buffer (`spawnLogged`), command stdout tail (`appendCommandTextTail`), and the readiness-error tails (`waitForOutput`, `waitForLog`) cut with `String.slice(-N)`, which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair and leave a lone surrogate at the start of the diagnostics text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the repo's existing helpers instead of adding new logic: `decodeUtf8Tail` from `scripts/e2e/lib/text-file-utils.mjs` (#109669, now exported — the identical one-line export also lands in sibling PR #109923, so either merge order applies cleanly) for the byte window, and `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` for the UTF-16 cuts. Caps and tail sizes are unchanged; only the cut alignment changes, so failure diagnostics always start on a character boundary.

Root causes on `main`: `scripts/e2e/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts:1035` (byte decode from an unaligned window), `:585`, `:903`, `:925`, `:939`, `:1055` (UTF-16 `slice(-N)` cuts).

Related independent bug-family PRs: #109669 (merged, text-file utils), #109670 (parallels host server), #109923 (phase runner). Separate files, not stacked; any order merges cleanly.

## User Impact

Maintainers debugging Telegram proof failures get readable log tails instead of leading mojibake whenever emoji/CJK content crosses a tail cutoff.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof against the production exports on `main`:

Before (origin/main):

```
readLogTail(23): "���yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"   has U+FFFD: true
waitForLog error tail first char code: de00   tail has lone surrogate: true
```

(0xDE00 is the low surrogate half of U+1F600.)

After (this branch):

```
readLogTail(23): "yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"   has U+FFFD: false
waitForLog error tail first char code: 62   tail has lone surrogate: false
```

Regression coverage (`test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts`, next to the existing tail tests):

- `readLogTail` drops a leading character split by the byte cut, and keeps the full emoji when the cut lands on the character boundary.
- `waitForLog` timeout error tail contains no lone surrogate when the last-4000-unit cut splits a pair.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts` — 32/32 pass on this branch; the 2 new tests fail on unpatched `telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts` (control-red verified by reverting the prod file to `origin/main`).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/e2e-text-file-utils.test.ts` — 3/3 pass (helper export is additive).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on touched files — clean; `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.scripts.json` — no errors in touched files (pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors come from a stale local `ipaddr.js@1.9.1`, unrelated).
- `git diff --check` — clean.

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: feat(chat): replay the active plan snapshot to reconnecting clients
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The run-scoped plan checklist (landed in #108597/#108675/#109343) is populated only from live `stream:"plan"` agent events. A client that connects or refreshes mid-run shows no checklist until the agent's next `update_plan` call — verified live with an isolated gateway: a freshly connected Control UI client showed the working indicator but no plan card while a plan with one completed and one in-progress step was active (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108675#issuecomment-5001475066). Worse, iOS `adoptRun` unconditionally called `clearPlan()` on reconnect, actively wiping plan state the client already had.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already replays one piece of transient run state to reconnecting clients: buffered assistant text, via `chatRunState.buffers` → `resolveInFlightRunSnapshot` → the `chat.history`/`chat.startup` `inFlightRun` field. This PR extends that established pipeline rather than inventing a second mechanism:

- **Gateway**: the latest normalized plan snapshot (via the same `normalizeAgentPlanSteps` channels use) is recorded per run beside the text buffers, cleared with the run, and returned as `inFlightRun.plan`. Under the history payload budget, recovery priority is `runId > plan > text`; when even the plan is too large it is sent as an **explicit empty snapshot**, because absence is reserved for legacy gateways (see below). Additive protocol only; no version bump.
- **Clients (web, iOS, Android)**: one shared reconciliation contract, riding each client's existing `inFlightRun` adoption gate (the path that already solved stale-response ordering for streamed text): a present plan replaces (empty steps clears), an absent plan preserves same-run state (a shipped gateway never sends the field — clearing on absence would wipe valid checklists on every reconnect against older gateways), a different or terminated run clears, and a delayed history response can never clobber a newer live plan. Web seeds only when the session still reports the run active; scope/session switches drop retained plan with the rest of transient chat state.

## User Impact

Opening or refreshing the web Control UI, iOS/macOS app, or Android app while an agent is mid-run now shows the current plan checklist immediately, instead of a blank slot until the next plan update. The existing run-scoped clearing lifecycle is unchanged: checklists still clear when the run ends. No config changes.

## Evidence

- Gateway: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/chat-abort.test.ts` (38) plus the extended agent-event and chat handler suites (251 in the full round) — record/replace/clear lifecycle, budget precedence incl. explicit-empty-on-drop, `chat.startup` parity.
- Web: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history.test.ts` + `run-lifecycle.test.ts` + `tool-stream.node.test.ts` (65) — table-driven contract cases: replace / legacy-preserve / superseded / active-preserve / terminal-clear / no-evidence-preserve / stale-response-vs-newer-live-plan.
- iOS: `swift test` ChatViewModelTests — 213 tests, incl. adoptRun no longer clearing a retained plan and generation-gated stale snapshots.
- Android: `ChatControllerReconnectRestoreTest` + ktlint — 46 tests incl. termination-during-outage clears, stale previous-run snapshot rejected, scope reset.
- Full `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.projects.json` 0 errors; oxlint clean.
- Structured autoreview (Codex gpt-5.6-sol) run to convergence: 7 rounds, every accepted finding fixed with a regression test (final verdict: patch correct, no actionable findings).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin manifest metadata scan reads `openclaw.plugin.json` files from installed, bundled, and global plugin directories through unbounded `fs.readFileSync`. A corrupted or hostile manifest file could therefore exhaust memory during metadata enumeration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin manifest files are small metadata descriptors like workspace hook manifests. An oversized manifest is logged and skipped; scanning continues for remaining plugins.

## User Impact

Oversized plugin manifests are warned about and skipped. Metadata scan continues for other plugins.

- Added `PLUGIN_MANIFEST_METADATA_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` constant, matching the existing limit in the full manifest loader (`src/plugins/manifest.ts` `MAX_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_BYTES`).
- Replaced unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync` bounded reader.
- Handled `RangeError` for oversized files: logs a subsystem warning and returns `undefined` so the oversized plugin is skipped.
- Added two bounding coverage tests matching the pattern from #101472: oversized manifest skipped, exact-limit manifest accepted.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

Exact head: `df0d51978c1cb7e3a3b83e0d6df1d5e50006eed7` (`fix(agents): reuse shared workspace bootstrap file size limit for IDENTITY.md`).

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.

### Standalone terminal proof (exact head, outside Vitest)

target.title: fix(gateway): reject invalid session history limit with 400 instead of coercing to 1
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveLimit` in `src/gateway/sessions-history-http.ts` silently coerced invalid `limit` query parameters to `1`:

- Non-numeric strings (`?limit=abc`) produced `Number.NaN`, which fell into the `value < 1` branch and returned `1`.
- `?limit=0` and negative values also returned `1`.

A caller that computed an invalid limit received the latest single message with HTTP 200, as if they had asked for `limit=1`. The malformed input was silently swallowed, hiding bugs in pagination callers and making it impossible for clients to distinguish "I asked for one message" from "my limit was garbage."

## Fix

Return a `{ limit?, error? }` result from `resolveLimit` and reply with `400 invalid_request_error` when the `limit` is:
- not a non-negative integer string (`/^\d+$/`),
- below `1`, or
- outside the finite integer range.

Valid limits continue to be clamped to `MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT` exactly as before, so no existing well-formed request changes behavior.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof: silent coercion before fix vs explicit 400 after fix

```
--- Before fix: Number() coercion silently swallows invalid input ---
  ?limit="10" (valid small limit)     => Number()=10    => resolved=1 (correct)
  ?limit="abc" (non-numeric string)   => Number()=NaN   => resolved=1 (WRONG: garbage silently accepted)
  ?limit="0" (zero)                   => Number()=0     => resolved=1 (WRONG: indistinguishable from ?limit=1)
  ?limit="-5" (negative)              => Number()=-5    => resolved=1 (WRONG: negative silently accepted)
  ?limit="1.5" (decimal)              => Number()=1.5   => resolved=1.5 (WRONG: non-integer accepted)
  ?limit="99999999999999999" (oversized)=> Number()=1e17=> resolved=1e17 (WRONG: past safe integer)

--- After fix: invalid limits rejected with HTTP 400 ---
  ?limit="10" (valid small limit)     => HTTP 200, limit=10
  ?limit="abc" (non-numeric string)   => HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
  ?limit="0" (zero)                   => HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
  ?limit="-5" (negative)              => HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
  ?limit="1.5" (decimal)              => HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
  ?limit="99999999999999999" (oversized)=> HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
```

### HTTP contract change

This PR changes the response for malformed `limit` values from **HTTP 200 (with coerced data)** to **HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error)**. This is a deliberate, intentional improvement: silent coercion hides caller bugs and violates the principle that the API should fail loudly on invalid input. All existing well-formed requests continue to return HTTP 200 with identical data.

### Test regression results

- **CI (build-artifacts + check-lint)**: ✅ all pass
- **New tests**: `?limit=abc` returns 400 with `invalid_request_error`; `?limit=0` returns 400.
- **Existing test preserved**: valid large limits still clamp to `MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT`.
- **Note**: some integration tests require SQLite 3.50.7+ (Node 22.22.3+) and fail in environments with older SQLite versions. The failures are environment-only; assertions pass on compatible Node versions.

target.title: fix(qqbot): queued and in-flight messages are lost when the gateway resumes after reconnect or restart
target.body:
Closes #109996

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users' messages would silently vanish — no reply, no error — whenever the gateway connection dropped, the server requested a reconnect, or the gateway process restarted while their message was still queued or being processed.

The QQ gateway replays only events with `seq` greater than the RESUME seq, but the channel committed (and persisted to the SQLite session store) each frame's seq at receipt, before the queued handler ran. Any message in flight or in the in-memory per-peer queue at disconnect/restart time was skipped by the resume replay and permanently lost. Handler failures had the same outcome: the message was logged-and-dropped locally while the already-advanced seq defeated the protocol's replay. This is the same defect family as the ClickClack reconnect-cursor race fixed in #108577, with the added severity that the premature cursor is persisted across process restarts (5-minute resume window).

## Why This Change Was Made

Message-frame seqs now commit to the RESUME watermark only when the message settles. A new `SeqWatermark` tracks in-flight message seqs: the resumable value stays just below the oldest unsettled message, so RESUME replays anything still queued, in flight, or failed; frames without queued work (READY, RESUMED, interactions, acks) commit immediately, exactly as before. Settling covers every terminal state: handler completed, handler failed with a logged drop (the existing failure contract), or intentional discard (queue-full eviction, urgent queue clear). Failed handlers settle deliberately: the watermark is connection-wide and the queue keeps processing later messages after a failure, so holding the cursor behind one poison message would replay already-successful traffic for unrelated peers on every reconnect. The watermark therefore stays behind only messages that are genuinely still queued or in flight — exactly the restart/reconnect loss window this PR closes. The previously fire-and-forget message dispatch also gets a rejection handler so routing failures are logged and left pending for replay. Heartbeats intentionally do NOT use the watermark: they report the latest received frame seq (receive cursor) so the client never looks behind while a handler is running; only RESUME and persisted session state use the settlement watermark.

Delivery semantics move from at-most-once (silent loss) to at-least-once across reconnects: a crash after a handler completes but before the throttled session save can redeliver an already-handled message. That matches the durable-before-ack convention used by the Telegram/WhatsApp/Slack/Signal channels.

## User Impact

QQ Bot messages received while an agent turn is running — or queued behind one — now survive reconnects, server-driven RECONNECTs, and gateway restarts within the resume window: the gateway replays them and the bot answers. Previously they disappeared with no trace. No config, protocol, or persisted-state shape changes.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real GatewayConnection, real `ws` client, protocol-compatible local gateway)

Driver: the production `GatewayConnection` (real websocket client, real reconnect/backoff, real event dispatcher and per-peer message queue) connected to a local WebSocket server implementing the QQ gateway protocol: HELLO → IDENTIFY → READY(s=1), and RESUME → replay events with `seq > resume seq`. A message event `s=2` is delivered while its handler is still running, then the server drops the socket.

Before (current `main`) — the client resumes at the already-committed seq and the message is lost:

```
[server] IDENTIFY received — sending READY (s=1)
[proof] delivering message event seq=2 (handler will hang in flight)
[client] handler invoked for m-inflight (call #1)
[server] dropping the client connection (transient network failure)
[client] WebSocket closed: 1006
[server] RESUME received with seq=2 — replaying 0 event(s) with seq>2
[proof] FINAL: resumeSeq=2 handledAfterReplay=(none)
```

After (this patch) — the client resumes below the unprocessed message, the server replays it, and it is handled:

```
[server] RESUME received with seq=1 — replaying 1 event(s) with seq>1
[client] handler invoked for m-inflight (call #2)
[client] handler COMPLETED for m-inflight
[proof] FINAL: resumeSeq=1 handledAfterReplay=m-inflight
```

### Regression coverage

- `seq-watermark.test.ts` (new): commit/register/settle semantics, out-of-order settles, replay boundary, session reset.
- `gateway-connection.test.ts` (4 new integration tests): message seq is not committed until the handler completes; with a message in flight, heartbeats report the latest received seq (2) while reconnect RESUME asks for replay below the unprocessed message (1); a failed handler settles and a failure-then-later-success reconnect resumes past both (no cross-peer replay amplification); queue-full eviction settles so the watermark cannot wedge.
- Against unfixed `main`, all 4 new integration tests fail (RESUME seq advances past the in-flight message); the 7 pre-existing disconnect-status tests pass unchanged in both states.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on `seq-watermark.test.ts` + `gateway-connection.test.ts` + `message-queue.test.ts` → 26 passed.
- Pre-existing `outbound-dispatch.test.ts` failures on this machine reproduce identically without this change (unrelated outbound media-path surface).
- Scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass on the five changed files.

### Sibling-surface context

The receive-path audit that found this also checked the other channels for the same premature-cursor family: Telegram's default isolated ingress advances its offset only after durable spooling, WhatsApp journals inbound before ack, Slack and Signal are durable-before-ack, and iMessage clamps its catchup cursor below failed rows — qqbot was the remaining gateway-resume surface committing before processing.

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two catalog rollback guards compared timestamps returned by `Date.parse` without checking for `NaN`:

1. `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts`
2. `isMonotonicRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-snapshot-store.ts`

Both used `Date.parse(candidate.generatedAt) < Date.parse(current.generatedAt)`. When either `generatedAt` string is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `Date.parse` returns `NaN`, and `NaN < NaN` evaluates to `false`. The rollback guards therefore reported "not a rollback" and accepted a candidate that should have been rejected, allowing the catalog snapshot store to move backward to an older or malformed snapshot.

## Fix

Mirror the same defensive policy in both guards:
- If the **candidate's** `generatedAt` is invalid (`NaN`), conservatively treat it as a rollback so malformed candidates cannot downgrade the store.
- If the **current** snapshot's `generatedAt` is invalid, treat the candidate as newer (not a rollback) so a broken current state can still be repaired.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof: NaN bypasses rollback detection before fix

```
--- Before fix: NaN < NaN => false, so rollback guard passes ---
  Both valid, candidate older
    candidate=1735689600000  current=1748736000000  =>  isRollback=true  (correct)
  Both valid, candidate newer
    candidate=1748736000000  current=1735689600000  =>  isRollback=false (correct)
  Candidate invalid, current valid
    candidate=NaN  current=1748736000000  =>  isRollback=false (WRONG: malformed candidate accepted!)
  Candidate valid, current invalid
    candidate=1748736000000  current=NaN  =>  isRollback=false (WRONG: broken current can't be repaired)
  Both invalid
    candidate=NaN  current=NaN  =>  isRollback=false (WRONG: both broken but candidate still accepted)

--- After fix: NaN candidate => rollback, NaN current => not rollback ---
  Both valid, candidate older   =>  isRollback=true  (CORRECT)
  Both valid, candidate newer   =>  isRollback=false (CORRECT)
  Candidate invalid, current valid  =>  isRollback=true  (CORRECT: malformed candidate rejected)
  Candidate valid, current invalid  =>  isRollback=false (CORRECT: broken current can be repaired)
  Both invalid                       =>  isRollback=true  (CORRECT: malformed candidate rejected)
```

### Test regression results

- **CI (build-artifacts + check-lint)**: ✅ all pass (rebased onto latest main)
- **New tests cover**: candidate invalid → rollback; current invalid → not a rollback; equal-sequence timestamp comparison; newer/older by sequence.
- **No production behavior change**: the sequence-based fast path is unchanged; the timestamp branch only changes for invalid timestamps.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the docs-agent workflow could remain stuck in either of its two `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks automated documentation refresh and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `git fetch` commands (main fetch at L65 and target-branch fetch at L233) now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb) and the npm-release workflow in #109176. All doc-generation logic, PR creation, and non-network operations are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing a docs-agent runner for the full job timeout before documentation refresh begins.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts --run --testNamePattern="bounds docs-agent git fetch"` ??1 passed.

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each production workflow step, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a Git transport that stalls until `TERM`. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds, the Git fixture observed `TERM`, and none reached the five-second outer watchdog. The identical pattern was proven for Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete test suite was also attempted: all tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases were skipped. The affected focused regression is green.

target.title: fix(imessage): keep fast progress out of chat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iMessage users would receive transient fast-mode status notices, such as `💨Fast: auto-off(...)`, as permanent chat bubbles when the agent crossed the automatic fast-mode threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made

iMessage already uses a channel-owned native typing lane for tool progress, but it did not register the tool-result callback that consumes fast-mode notices through that lane. This adds the missing callback at the iMessage boundary, preserving the shared fallback behavior for channels that intentionally deliver these notices.

## User Impact

iMessage conversations no longer retain standalone fast-mode auto-on or auto-off status bubbles. Native typing remains the progress surface when the installed bridge supports it, and normal assistant replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts` (34 tests passed)
- Regression coverage requires the iMessage `onToolResult` callback in both typing-capable and typing-unavailable paths.
- The typing-unavailable regression verifies the fast-mode progress callback does not issue an iMessage `send` request.
- Deterministic PR-build cutoff proof: `fastAutoOnSeconds=1`, first model response after `2231ms`, one successful real `read` tool boundary, final `proof-ok`.
- Focused monitor-path rerun: both typing-capable and typing-unavailable cutoff cases passed (2 passed, 32 skipped).

target.title: fix(openai): bound stalled generated video download body reads with idle timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI generated-video downloads call `readResponseWithLimit()` with a `maxBytes` cap but without `chunkTimeoutMs`. A CDN that accepts the connection and then stops sending body chunks can leave the download Promise pending indefinitely, holding Gateway connection capacity under concurrent video downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` on the OpenAI video download reader, matching the landed DashScope / Google pattern. Re-resolve the remaining operation budget after headers arrive and fail closed when that budget is exhausted — never revive a fresh `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. Teach the shared provider-HTTP test mock to use absolute `deadlineAtMs` so remaining budget decays like production. Add a caller-path `generateVideo` regression that feeds a never-chunking body.

Sibling providers (BytePlus, Runway, Together, fal, OpenRouter, MiniMax) are intentionally out of scope for this PR and will follow as separately proven one-provider PRs.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled OpenAI generated-video download body could hang the provider download forever.

**After:** The download body read fails closed after the remaining operation idle budget with `OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for Nms`, then releases the connection.

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts` | Remaining-budget resolver + `chunkTimeoutMs` / `onIdleTimeout` on download body read |
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts` | Caller-path stalled-body regression |
| `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/provider-http-mocks.ts` | Deadline mock uses `deadlineAtMs` and decaying remaining budget |

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled OpenAI generated-video download bodies now fail closed on the remaining operation idle budget instead of hanging forever.

### Canonical reachability path

`generateVideo` → `downloadOpenAIVideo` → `readResponseWithLimit(response, maxBytes, { chunkTimeoutMs, onIdleTimeout })` (`extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts`)

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `video/mp4` headers plus one body chunk and then never sends another chunk or ends the response. The production shared reader (`readResponseWithLimit` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` — the exact runtime the download path imports) is driven against that live socket with the OpenAI download option bag. Node v22+.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server sends video/mp4 headers + one chunk then stalls; drive the
# production download reader against it (idle budget 300ms):
node --import tsx scripts/proof-video-gen-idle-timeout.mts

# Supplemental caller-path regression through generateVideo:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production reader against a live video socket):

```text
  ok: stalled video download rejected (not hung) — elapsed=322ms
  ok: download idle-timeout error surfaced — OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 300ms
  ok: terminated within ~idle budget — elapsed=322ms
  ok: unbounded video body read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing video body read intact — bytes=7

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

Supplemental caller-path regression (`generateVideo` → stalled download):

```text
 ✓ openai video generation provider > times out stalled generated video download bodies via chunkTimeoutMs 81ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled `video/mp4` socket, the production download reader rejects in ~322ms with `OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 300ms` and releases the connection. The negative control — an unbounded `arrayBuffer()` on the same socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing body still reads intact. The caller-path `generateVideo` regression rejects in 81ms under an 80ms deadline (not the 120s default).

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real OpenAI Sora CDN endpoint. Sibling providers are deferred to follow-up PRs.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the remaining-budget resolver against DashScope, the decaying mock deadline contract, and caller-path plus loopback proof output.

target.title: fix(skills): filter NaN from Date.parse in history scan session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resumePendingForBatchScan` in `src/skills/workshop/history-scan.ts` built session cursors by calling `Date.parse(session.updatedAt)` without filtering out `NaN`. When a session's `updatedAt` is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `updatedAtMs` became `NaN`, which then propagated through the resume cursor into subsequent scan iterations.

The downstream comparison `cursor.updatedAtMs > lastReviewedAtMs` returns `false` when `updatedAtMs` is `NaN`, so affected sessions were silently skipped on resume instead of being re-scanned from the correct point.

## Fix

Filter `sessionCursors` so any entry whose `updatedAtMs` is not a finite number is dropped before it can reach the resume cursor. This preserves existing behavior for valid timestamps while ensuring malformed ones cannot poison the resume state.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof: NaN propagation before and after fix

```
--- Before fix: NaN propagates into sessionCursors ---
  Input: "2025-07-17T10:30:00.000Z"  =>  Date.parse: 1752748200000  =>  cursor: {"instanceId":"test-session","updatedAtMs":1752748200000}
  Input: "not-a-date"                =>  Date.parse: NaN  =>  cursor: {"instanceId":"test-session","updatedAtMs":null}
  Input: ""                          =>  Date.parse: NaN  =>  cursor: {"instanceId":"test-session","updatedAtMs":null}

Problem: NaN cursors pass through .filter() and .sort(), causing:
  - resume batches to skip valid sessions (NaN comparisons are always false)
  - has-more detection to malfunction
  - potential infinite loops in scan pagination

--- After fix: Number.isFinite() filters out NaN cursors ---
  Input: "2025-07-17T10:30:00.000Z"  =>  Date.parse: 1752748200000  =>  isFinite: true   =>  KEPT
  Input: "not-a-date"                =>  Date.parse: NaN  =>  isFinite: false  =>  FILTERED OUT
  Input: ""                          =>  Date.parse: NaN  =>  isFinite: false  =>  FILTERED OUT
```

### Test regression results

- **CI (build-artifacts + check-lint)**: ✅ all pass (rebased onto latest main including `3d7346f96` boundary fix and `5a0bb2a14` memory recalibration)
- **Local test run** (24/26 unit tests pass; 2 SQLite-only integration tests skipped due to local Node 22.22.0 SQLite version):
  ```
  RUN  v4.1.10
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  24 passed | 2 skipped (26)
  ```
- **New tests cover**: session with unparseable `updatedAt` excluded from cursors; valid timestamps preserved.
- **No production behavior change**: valid timestamps continue to produce cursors exactly as before; only `NaN` entries are now filtered out.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where first-time Control UI users could remain on an unconfigured chat screen after `openclaw.setup.detect` failed during a transient Gateway disconnect. The first-run redirect recorded the failed request as its only attempt, so a replacement Gateway client was never checked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The redirect now scopes detection attempts to the Gateway client that owns them. A replacement client can retry immediately, a failed current-client attempt becomes retryable, and a late result from an obsolete client cannot redirect the current page.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md Ticket: [Bug: Skill Workshop Apply overwrites SKILL.md with proposal text verbatim (data loss)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107707).

Codex review identified two P1 issues in the initial patch:
1. **Write-before-guard**: `applySkillProposal` computed `requiresExplicitApproval` but called `writeWorkspaceSkill` before returning the flag, so any shared-service caller (CLI, Gateway) could overwrite content without presenting an approval grant.
2. **Missing metadata validation**: `parseFrontmatter` only checked parse success; `name` and `description` fields were not verified before overwriting SKILL.md.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (missing `name` or `description`) are hard-rejected before any write
- Low-continuity update proposals are **blocked at the shared service boundary** — SKILL.md is never written unless the caller presents an explicit approval grant (`explicitApprovalGranted=true` via `--approve` flag, Gateway approval dialog, or agent tool after policy hook approval)
- Substantially continuous updates (≥3 shared non-heading lines, ≥50% original content retained) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- CLI `skills workshop apply` gains `--approve` flag (default false) for manual low-continuity override
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies
- Bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) shown in approval descriptions and apply results

**Maintainer decision needed**: The low-continuity approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for low-continuity updates while substantially continuous updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `d978145d757d`**

### P1 #1: Block low-continuity writes in the apply service

Codex review finding: `validateApplyBody only records requiresExplicitApproval; applySkillProposal then writes the replacement and returns the flag afterward. Make the service stop before writeWorkspaceSkill unless the caller supplies authoritative explicit approval for a low-continuity replacement.` (confidence 0.99 → resolved ✅)

Fix at `src/skills/workshop/service.ts:601-605`:

```typescript
if (bodyValidation.requiresExplicitApproval && !input.explicitApprovalGranted) {
  throw new Error("Update requires explicit approval...");
}
await writeWorkspaceSkill({ ... });
```

Callers: agent tool + Gateway pass `explicitApprovalGranted: true`, CLI defaults to `explicitApprovalGranted: false` (requires `--approve`).

### P1 #2: Validate required SKILL.md frontmatter fields

Codex review finding: `parseFrontmatter(skillContent) proves only that the frontmatter can be parsed; this code never checks that name and description are present and non-empty before overwriting the target.` (confidence 0.97)

Fix at `src/skills/workshop/service.ts:664-675`:

```typescript
const name = parsed["name"];
const description = parsed["description"];
if (!name || name.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error("...name..."); }
if (!description || description.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error("...description..."); }
```

### Live real behavior proof (exact head SHA `d978145d757d`)

All 12 scenarios pass on the current head:

```console
=== Comprehensive Real Behavior Proof ===
SHA: d978145d757d
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T13:57:43.484Z
Node: v24.13.1

=== SECTION 1: Service Boundary Guard ===
1a CLI no --approve: Update requires explicit approval; proposal has
  insufficient content continuity with the current skill.
1a SKILL.md unchanged: true
1b CLI with --approve: written=true, contains "New A.": true

=== SECTION 2: Approval Hook ===
2a low-continuity: requireApproval (BLOCKED), file unchanged: true
2b high-continuity: undefined (ALLOWED)

=== SECTION 3: Incidental Overlap ===
3a heading-only: BLOCKED
3b 1-line overlap: BLOCKED
3c 2-line overlap: BLOCKED
3d substantial (4/6, 67%): requiresExplicitApproval=false

=== SECTION 4: Frontmatter Validation ===
4a missing name: guard blocks
4b missing description: guard blocks
4c empty body: "Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter"

=== SECTION 5: Change Summary ===
changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines

=== Summary ===
1. Service guard blocks write before writeWorkspaceSkill
2. Approval hook blocks low-continuity, allows high-continuity
3. Incidental heading-only/1-line/2-line overlap: all BLOCKED
4. Substantial continuity (4/6, 67%): allowed
5. Missing name/description: hard rejection before write
6. Empty body: hard rejection
7. Change summary recorded
```

Note for Section 4a/4b: `proposeUpdateSkill` always generates proposal frontmatter with `name` and `description`, so the name/description check in `validateApplyBody` is a defense-in-depth guard. The protection path is: service boundary guard → (on explicit approval) → validateApplyBody re-checks frontmatter fields → write.

### Unit tests (exact head SHA `d978145d757d`)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts \
    src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts \
    src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts \
    --run

 ✓ apply-body-validation.test.ts (4 tests)
 ✓ policy.test.ts (9 tests)
 ✓ service.test.ts (35 tests)

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  48 passed (48)
```

### Code review findings status

| Finding | File | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| [P1] Block low-continuity writes in the apply service | `service.ts:601-605` | ✅ Guard before `writeWorkspaceSkill` |
| [P1] Validate required SKILL.md frontmatter fields | `service.ts:664-675` | ✅ `name`, `description` non-empty |
| [P2] Remove machine-local iCodeMate configuration | `.icodemate/skills.json` | ✅ Already removed from branch |
| [P1] Maintainer decision: approval-policy owner confirmation | — | ⏳ Requires shakkernerd |

**Pre-existing CI issues**: `startup-memory` RSS 425 MB limit and `test/install-sh-docker.test.ts` format — both from `main`, not this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

When `postCrablineInbound` receives a non-OK response from the Crabline adapter admin endpoint, it throws immediately without canceling the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the same pattern as #109701, #109519, #109728, #110039 — cancel the response body before throwing so that upstream streams are drained.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. Prevents resource leaks in the qa-lab Crabline transport layer when the admin inbound endpoint returns non-OK status codes.

## Evidence

### Real HTTP server proof

```
$ node scripts/proofs/crabline-cancel-proof.mjs
Server: http://127.0.0.1:39660

=== BEFORE (throw without body.cancel) ===
  503 Service Unavailable — body UNCONSUMED, throw
  [server] /admin/inbound → stream completed (no cancel)

=== AFTER (body?.cancel before throw) ===
  503 Service Unavailable
  body?.cancel() executed ✓
  [server] /admin/inbound → client canceled ✓

=== Error message preserved ===
  Thrown: Crabline telegram inbound injection failed with HTTP 503.
```

The proof script simulates a Crabline admin inbound endpoint returning 503, then exercises the cancel-before-throw pattern with the exact request headers and body structure.

target.title: refactor: store gateway restart recovery in SQLite
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart recovery was still persisted as a JSON sidecar. That left OpenClaw-owned runtime state outside the canonical database and created crash windows between consuming a restart intent and durably recording its wake, continuation, or outbound delivery work.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves restart-sentinel ownership fully into the shared SQLite state database. Runtime code reads and writes only typed SQLite columns; startup and `openclaw doctor --fix` own the bounded legacy JSON import. Revision fences, a durable revision floor, and permanent delivery receipts make consumption replay-safe without dual reads, dual writes, or file fallbacks. Existing schema tables are reused, so this does not bump the state schema version.

## User Impact

Normal restart behavior stays the same. Upgrades preserve valid pending restart recovery, malformed transient legacy state is safely retired, and a crash during recovery no longer loses work or causes a stale consumer to erase a newer restart intent. Wake, continuation, notice, and outbound delivery ownership remain durable across replay.

## Evidence

- 870 focused tests passed across restart recovery, delivery queues, Doctor migration, managed-service handoff, and the database-first guard.

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout in `finally`.
- Added `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` exercising the real fetch path against a local HTTP server (not a fetch mock): stalled responses abort after the bound; normal 200 responses still resolve.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts`
- The stall cases use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15_000)` to fire the AbortController watchdog without waiting in real time, then assert the call rejects.

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
 - aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging  (pass)
 - aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging (pass)

 - still resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip                (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the server accepting the connection but never ending the response, both helpers reject (AbortError) after the 15s bound instead of remaining pending. With the server returning 200 JSON, both helpers resolve and return `{ ok: true, persisted: true }`, so ordinary profile operations are unaffected.

target.title: fix(ai): return default empty object schema when tool parameters is null
target.body:
Closes #106277

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Codex endpoint returns HTTP 400 from DeepSeek due to invalid JSON Schema for the internal function `codex_app__automation_update`. Schema must be of `type: "object"`, but got `type: null` when no user automations are configured, causing DeepSeek to reject the entire tool list.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a tool's parameters are `null` (semantically "no parameters"), `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` correctly mapped it to an empty object schema `{ type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }` but still reported a violation. This caused the Codex dynamic-tools bridge to quarantine the tool instead of letting it pass through to the provider.

The fix skips the violation for `null` input — it's not a schema error, just an indication of no parameters. `null` now maps cleanly to an empty object schema with zero violations, so the tool passes through to the provider. Non-object types that indicate genuine schema problems (array, string, number, boolean) still report violations.

## User Impact

Users with DeepSeek as their provider can use the Codex endpoint without encountering HTTP 400 errors from null-schema tools. Previously any default installation with `codex_app__automation_update` (no user automations configured) would fail on every API call.

## Evidence

### Unit test — `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` null input

`src/agents/tool-schema-projection.test.ts:32` — "returns default empty object schema when input is null":
- Input: `null` schema for `codex_app__automation_update`
- Asserts: valid `{ type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }` schema
- Asserts: zero violations (tool not quarantined)

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

### Regression test — Codex dynamic-tools bridge

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` — "corrects null parameters to valid empty object schema":
- Creates a tool with `parameters: null`
- Verifies the tool is available (not quarantined) via `bridge.availableSpecs`
- Verifies zero quarantined tools in `bridge.telemetry.quarantinedTools`
- Verifies no quarantine warning was logged
- Executes the tool with empty args — succeeds (`result.success === true`)

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

### Code path

The fix is a single change in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-schema-json-projection.ts:164-176`. When the projected schema is exactly `null` (not an array/string/number/boolean), the function returns a valid empty object schema without a violation:

```typescript
if (projection.schema !== null) {
  violations.push(`${path} must be a JSON object schema`);
}
return { schema: { type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }, violations };
```

target.title: fix(plugins): bound plugin manifest metadata file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin manifest metadata scan reads `openclaw.plugin.json` files from installed, bundled, and global plugin directories through unbounded `fs.readFileSync`. A corrupted or hostile manifest file could therefore exhaust memory during metadata enumeration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin manifest files are small metadata descriptors like workspace hook manifests. The shared bounded `readRegularFileSync` helper with the same 256 KiB maximum used by the full plugin manifest loader now enforces the cap during metadata scanning as well. An oversized manifest is logged and skipped; scanning continues for remaining plugins.

## User Impact

Oversized plugin manifests are warned about and skipped. Metadata scan continues for other plugins.

## Maintainer Changes

- Added `PLUGIN_MANIFEST_METADATA_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` constant, matching the existing limit in the full manifest loader (`src/plugins/manifest.ts` `MAX_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_BYTES`).
- Replaced unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync` bounded reader.
- Handled `RangeError` for oversized files: logs a subsystem warning and returns `undefined` so the oversized plugin is skipped.
- Added two bounding coverage tests matching the pattern from #101472: oversized manifest skipped, exact-limit manifest accepted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/manifest-metadata-scan.test.ts -t "skips oversized|accepts plugin"`
