target.title: fix(onboarding): stop recommending tools setup cannot activate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the no-AI onboarding state told users to install Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, or Grok Build and then "check again", even though guided setup cannot turn those installations into a verified inference route. Pi and OpenCode are explicitly classified as unavailable whole-agent/ACP routes, Gemini CLI is excluded from the tool-free setup probe, and Kimi/Grok CLI installs have no guided detection path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recommendation catalog introduced in #109681 is shared by CLI, macOS, and Control UI, so correcting its inclusion policy fixes every surface at the source. The catalog now contains only Ollama and LM Studio (`appGuidedDiscovery`) plus Claude Code and Codex CLI (native setup candidates); the removed tools remain supported through their existing provider, OAuth, or ACP-specific flows.

Changing the empty-state wording would still steer users into a non-working check-again loop, while adding a second runtime filter would duplicate the detector's capability policy.

## Direct Codex dependency contract

I inspected sibling `openai/codex` source at `315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304` rather than relying on OpenClaw wrappers:

- `codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs:515` defines the `codex app-server` command and `codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs:1117` starts the production stdio app-server when no tooling subcommand is supplied.
- `codex-rs/cli/src/login.rs:424` implements `codex login status` by loading the configured auth store; success exits 0 and missing auth exits 1.
- `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs:38` defines the canonical `auth.json` token container, while `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs:427` proves auto mode prefers keyring and falls back to `auth.json`. This matches OpenClaw s non-prompting status probe and file-reader fallback.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:1161` registers stable `account/read`; `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs:993` resolves and returns the active provider account state.

These contracts confirm the retained Codex CLI recommendation has an installable command, a native authentication status path across Codex-owned stores, and a usable app-server account/runtime surface.

## User Impact

Fresh setup users now see four install suggestions that can lead directly to a setup candidate OpenClaw can test and persist. This does not remove Pi, OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, or xAI support; it only stops presenting their standalone CLI installs as fixes for the guided inference empty state.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Empty-state recommendations no longer include tool installs that guided setup cannot activate or verify.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, commit `84fdce9317db` on branch `fix/setup-recommend-usable-routes`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-recommended-installs.mts` - imports the production catalog loader, prints the returned IDs, and rejects any of the five unusable setup recommendations.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  PASS ids=ollama,lmstudio,claude-code,codex-cli unusable=none
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All clients receive only the four setup-compatible install cards from `recommendedInstalls`.
- **What was not tested:** The external installers and provider login flows were not executed because this patch changes only presentation catalog eligibility; existing dedicated support paths are untouched.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/recommended-tool-installs.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       110 passed (110)

$ OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- scripts/lib/recommended-tool-installs.json src/plugins/recommended-tool-installs.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts
EXIT=0

$ git diff --check
EXIT=0
```

The catalog regression failed before the JSON change by returning all nine IDs. `check:changed` first attempted its normal Blacksmith Testbox delegation; the host lacked the `blacksmith` executable, so trusted-source validation followed the documented local fallback and passed conflict, ratchet, dependency, format, boundary, typecheck, core lint, and script lint gates.

Structured Codex autoreview was attempted after the rebase with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --stream-engine-output`; the review transport returned HTTP 403 from `wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses` before a model response. The catalog producer, setup detector, all three client consumers, retained discovery contracts, removed tools dedicated paths, and direct Codex dependency source were reviewed manually.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - five misleading install cards are removed from the no-AI empty state.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config shape, persistence, default, or migration changes.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - no installer, auth, network, or execution code changes.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - existing tool/provider support and plugin contracts remain unchanged.
- Highest-risk area: Narrowing a centrally curated product recommendation list could reduce discovery of tools that still work through separate advanced flows.
- Mitigation: Eligibility is limited to current guided-setup candidate contracts; dedicated Pi/OpenCode ACP and Gemini/Kimi/xAI provider paths remain available elsewhere.

target.title: fix(voice-call): unref ngrok startup timeout and mark closed on timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`startNgrokTunnel`'s 30s startup `setTimeout` was never `unref()`'d, so an abandoned tunnel promise kept the host process alive until the timer fired. On the timeout path the child was killed but `closed` was not set, leaving the `stop()` cleanup path inconsistent with the eventual `close` event.

## Why This Change Was Made

`unref()` the startup timer so it cannot pin the event loop, and mark the process `closed` on timeout so `stop()` does not try to re-kill an already-terminating child.

## User Impact

The voice-call tunnel startup no longer holds the process open when its caller has moved on; no change to successful tunnel startup.

## Evidence

- Regression test "unrefs the ngrok startup timeout so it cannot keep the host process alive": spies on `setTimeout` and asserts the returned timer's `unref()` is called. **Red before the fix** (`unref` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.test.ts` → 16 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` is byte-identical for this region (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `startNgrokTunnel` in `extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.ts` started a 30s ngrok-startup timeout with `setTimeout` but never unref'd it, so the host process could be kept alive solely by the pending timer. The fix calls `timeout.unref()` and also marks the tunnel `closed` in the timeout branch before killing the process.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed timer/unref path is driven through a mocked ngrok child process so the exact `unref()` call is asserted without spawning a real tunnel.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.test.ts`

Evidence after fix (CI `Real behavior proof` job passed; local suite asserts):
```
- "unrefs the ngrok startup timeout so it cannot keep the host process alive" -> setTimeout's unref() called
```

Observed result after fix: The 30s startup watchdog no longer holds the event loop open, and the timeout branch now marks the tunnel closed before killing the process. The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head.

What was not tested: A real ngrok subprocess and live tunnel was not started (ngrok is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — `timeout.unref()` and the `closed` flag in the timeout branch — which are process/timer-control contracts.

target.title: fix(qqbot): cancel non-OK direct-upload response body before throwing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`downloadDirectUploadUrl` in the QQ Bot media module fetches media from direct-upload URLs through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. When the upstream returns a non-OK response, the code throws immediately without canceling the response body — the unconsumed stream holds a connection open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the same pattern as #109519 (Google Chat), #109508 (docs search), #109701 (MSTeams), #109728 (APNs relay), and #110039 (Telegram media harness) — cancel the response body before throwing so that upstream streams are drained.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. Prevents resource leaks when QQ Bot direct-upload URLs return non-OK HTTP status codes.

## Evidence

### Real HTTP server proof

```
$ node scripts/proofs/qqbot-direct-upload-cancel-proof.mjs
Server: http://127.0.0.1:36215

=== BEFORE (throw without body.cancel) ===
  503 Service Unavailable — body UNCONSUMED

=== AFTER (body?.cancel before throw) ===
  503 Service Unavailable
  body?.cancel() executed ✓
  [server] /direct-upload → client canceled stream ✓

=== PR diff (media.ts:163) ===
  if (!response.ok) {
+   await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
    throw new Error(`Failed to download direct upload...`);
```

The proof script starts a real HTTP server returning 503 with a slow binary stream (simulating a QQ Bot direct-upload response), then exercises the exact cancel-before-throw pattern. The server confirms `client canceled stream ✓`.

### Unit test

New test ("cancels a non-OK direct-upload response body before throwing") in `media.test.ts` verifies:
- A real `Response` with status 503 is returned by the fetch mock
- `response.body.cancel()` is called exactly once before the error is thrown
- Token acquisition is NOT attempted after the error

## What Problem This Solves

`FeishuStreamingSession` makes HTTP requests to the Feishu/Lark API through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. When the API returns a non-OK response, the code throws immediately without canceling the response body. Three sites are affected: the shared card-operation helper (covers update, replace, note, close), the tenant-token request, and the card-create request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the same pattern as #109519 (Google Chat), #109508 (docs search), #109701 (MSTeams), and #109728 (APNs relay) — cancel the response body before throwing so that upstream streams are drained and connections released.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. Prevents resource leaks when Feishu/Lark API returns non-OK status codes for streaming card operations.

## Evidence

### Real HTTP server proof

```
$ node scripts/proofs/feishu-streaming-card-cancel-proof.mjs
Server: http://127.0.0.1:35958

=== BEFORE (throw without body.cancel) ===
  503 Service Unavailable — body UNCONSUMED, no cancel

=== AFTER (body?.cancel before throw) ===
```

### Unit tests

target.title: fix(telegram): cancel unread response body on media fetch error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `defaultReadRemoteMediaBuffer` in the Telegram e2e harness receives a non-OK response (e.g. 404, 503), it throws immediately without canceling the response body. The unconsumed stream holds a connection open until garbage collection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the same pattern as #109519 (Google Chat), #109508 (docs search), #109677 (Chutes), #109701 (MSTeams consent upload), and #109728 (APNs relay) — cancel the response body before throwing so that upstream streams are drained and connections released.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. This is test harness infrastructure used by the Telegram bot media e2e tests. Prevents resource leaks from unconsumed response bodies.

## Evidence

### Real HTTP server proof

```
$ node scripts/proofs/telegram-media-cancel-proof.mjs
Server: http://127.0.0.1:34072

=== BEFORE (no body.cancel — throw immediately) ===
  Response: 503 Service Unavailable

=== AFTER (body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined) before throw) ===
  Response: 503 Service Unavailable
  body?.cancel() executed ✓
  [server] /new → client canceled stream ✓

=== Error message preserved after cancel ===
  Thrown: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:34072/error: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
```

The proof script starts a real HTTP server returning 503 with a slow stream, then exercises the exact cancel-before-throw pattern from this PR. The server confirms the client canceled the stream (`client canceled stream ✓`), demonstrating that `body?.cancel()` reaches the server and releases the connection. The error message is preserved after cancel.

### Unit test

New test ("cancels response body on non-ok status before throwing") in `bot.media.stickers-and-fragments.e2e.test.ts` verifies:
- A real `Response` with status 404 is returned by the fetch mock
- `response.body.cancel()` is called exactly once before the error is thrown
- Uses `ReadableStream({ cancel })` spy pattern as in #109701

target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` spawns a **detached** child (non-Windows) but never `unref()`s it and never removes the `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners on `close`. On the success path the promise resolves while the detached process and its pipe listeners stay attached, so the parent's event loop cannot exit until the child exits.

## Why This Change Was Made

`unref()` the child after spawn so a completed qa cli run does not keep the caller alive, and remove the data listeners on `close` so the resolved stream is not retained.

## User Impact

QA Lab suite runs and the host process can exit promptly after a qa cli invocation completes; no change to success/failure behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression test "unrefs the detached child so it cannot keep the parent event loop alive": asserts `child.unref()` is called once and stdio `data` listeners are detached on `close`. **Red before the fix** (`unref` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.test.ts` → 28 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` is byte-identical for this region (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` spawns a detached qa-cli child but never `unref()`s it and never removes the stdout/stderr `data` listeners on close, so the parent's event loop could stay alive (or retain the resolved stream) after the promise settles. The fix calls `child.unref()` and detaches both listeners in the `close` handler.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed spawn/unref/listener path is driven through a mocked `node:child_process` so the exact `child.unref()` call and listener detachment are asserted without spawning real processes.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.test.ts`

Evidence after fix (CI `Real behavior proof` job passed; local suite asserts):
```
- "unrefs the detached child so it cannot keep the parent event loop alive" -> child.unref called exactly once
- stdout/stderr data listeners removed on close so the resolved stream is not retained
```

Observed result after fix: The detached child is unref'd exactly once and both stream listeners are detached on `close`, so the caller can exit without reaping or retaining the child. The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head.

What was not tested: A real subprocess spawn against a live qa-cli binary was not executed (the spawn is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — the `unref()` call and listener cleanup — which are process-control contracts, not business logic.

target.title: fix(approval): preserve Unicode in native-route approval slug truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When exec approval command IDs contain multi-byte Unicode characters near the 8-character slug boundary, raw `.slice(0, 8)` could split UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing garbled short codes in user-facing approval notices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, matching the pattern already used in `src/logging/redact.ts` and `src/tui/tui-local-shell.ts`.

## User Impact

Approval fallback notices (`/approve <slug> <decisions>`) will display correct Unicode characters instead of potentially corrupted short codes.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (9 passed, 1 file)
```
 ✓ labels approver-DM-only delivery as channel DMs
 ✓ labels mixed-surface delivery as the channel itself
 ✓ reports sorted unique destinations
 ✓ suppresses the notice when there are no destinations
 ✓ shortens exec approval ids to an 8-char slug
 ✓ keeps short exec ids unshortened
 ✓ keeps plugin approval ids unshortened regardless of length
 ✓ does not produce a lone surrogate when an emoji straddles the 8-char slug boundary
 ✓ preserves an emoji fully within the 8-char slug boundary
```

### Test Coverage
- **Straddling surrogate pair**: 🦞 (U+1F99E) at position 7-8 of a 9+ char exec id — verifies no lone high surrogate (0xD800–0xDBFF) in the slug
- **Emoji within limit**: 🦞 at positions 6-7 (within 8-char boundary) — verified preserved in "/approve" output
- **Short ids**: exec ids ≤ 8 chars and all plugin ids kept unshortened

### Real Environment Behavior Proof

Terminal transcript of the fix running against the real `sliceUtf16Safe` dependency in the OpenClaw development environment (`script -q` recorded, executed via `tsx`):

```
─── Scenario 1: Emoji straddles 8-char boundary ─────────────────────
  Input exec approval ID:  "1234567🦞extra"
  ❌ OLD: .slice(0, 8) → "1234567\ud83e"  ⚠️ LONE SURROGATE!
  ✅ NEW: sliceUtf16Safe → "1234567"       ✓ OK

─── Scenario 2: Emoji fully within 8-char boundary ──────────────────
  Input exec approval ID:  "123456🦞extra"
  OLD: .slice(0, 8)  → "123456🦞" ✓
  NEW: sliceUtf16Safe → "123456🦞" ✓

─── Scenario 3: Short exec ID (≤ 8 chars) kept unshortened ─────────
  Input exec approval ID:  "abc12345"
  OLD: .slice(0, 8)  → "abc12345" ✓
  NEW: sliceUtf16Safe → "abc12345" ✓

─── Scenario 4: Plugin approval ID never shortened ──────────────────
  Input plugin approval ID: "very-long-plugin-id-that-should-never-be-truncated"
  Plugin ID not truncated ✓

─── Scenario 5: CJK characters near boundary ────────────────────────
  Input exec approval ID:  "审批审批审批extra"
  OLD: .slice(0, 8) → "审批审批审批ex"  ✓ (BMP, no surrogate issue)
  NEW: sliceUtf16Safe → "审批审批审批ex"  ✓
```

**Key finding**: Old `.slice(0, 8)` produces a lone high surrogate (0xD83E) when 🦞 (U+1F99E, surrogate pair 🦞) straddles the 8-char boundary. The new `sliceUtf16Safe` correctly adjusts the boundary to avoid splitting surrogate pairs, producing clean Unicode output.

target.title: feat(plugin-sdk): onModelDiagnosticEvent for trusted model.* events
target.body:
## Why

Plugins subscribing to diagnostic events via `onDiagnosticEvent` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/diagnostic-runtime`) never see the `model.*` lifecycle. The public API filter at [`src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts:879-886`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts#L879-L886):

```ts
export function onDiagnosticEvent(listener: (evt: DiagnosticEventPayload) => void): () => void {
  return onInternalDiagnosticEvent((event, metadata) => {
    if (metadata.trusted || event.type === "log.record") {
      return;
    }
    listener(event);
  });
}
```

drops **every** event whose dispatcher metadata is `trusted: true`. The runtime emits `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, `model.call.error`, `model.usage`, and `model.failover` via `emitTrustedDiagnosticEvent`. So the entire model lifecycle is invisible to plugins.

This breaks observability/cost-attribution plugins. A telemetry bridge plugin needs:

- `model.call.completed` (provider/model identity) to populate per-call span attributes
- `model.usage` (token counts, cost) for per-call attribution

Today both subscriptions are dead code against the trusted emit paths. Concretely, the embedded codex/Responses runner emits the full model lifecycle via `emitTrustedDiagnosticEvent` (see `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.ts`), but no plugin listener ever receives any of it — model traffic on the dashboard side ends up bucketed as "unknown" instead of `gpt-5.5`/etc.

## Approach

Add a focused, opt-in plugin-sdk API `onModelDiagnosticEvent` that exposes exactly the five model lifecycle event types — and only those — to plugins. The general `onDiagnosticEvent` filter is unchanged: it still drops trusted events, so the safety contract of the broad subscription is preserved. Plugins that want model telemetry have to opt in explicitly.

The new helper otherwise mirrors `onDiagnosticEvent`'s contract (cloned-and-frozen payloads, isolated listener failures, unsubscribe disposer).

A module-local allowlist (`PLUGIN_VISIBLE_TRUSTED_MODEL_EVENT_TYPES`) documents which event types are reachable through this API and is the single place to update if more model lifecycle types are added later.

## Files

- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` — add `onModelDiagnosticEvent` + allowlist (+45 lines)
- `src/plugin-sdk/{diagnostic-runtime,index,compat}.ts` — re-export the new function so plugins can `import { onModelDiagnosticEvent } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/diagnostic-runtime"` (or the top-level barrel / compat subpath)
- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts` — three new tests:
  1. delivers all five `model.*` trusted types and filters non-model traffic
  2. the original `onDiagnosticEvent` still hides model events from plugins (defends the safety contract)
  3. unsubscribe disposer stops further delivery
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased / Changes entry

Total: 6 files, +158 / −2.

## Tests

- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts`: 22/22 passing
- Plugin-SDK guardrail tests (`src/plugins/loader-sdk-import-guardrails.test.ts`, `src/plugins/contracts/plugin-sdk-root-alias.test.ts`): 44 tests, all passing

## End-to-end validation

Built a full `dist/` from this branch, swapped it into a deployed gateway, and ran a real codex (`openai-codex/gpt-5.5`) turn from a Telegram-driven session. Bridge plugin logs show **both** subscriptions on startup:

```
[agentweave-bridge] subscribed to diagnostic events via plugin-sdk
[agentweave-bridge] subscribed to model.* trusted events via plugin-sdk
```

…and during the turn the bridge now receives the `model.usage` event for codex/gpt-5.5 (previously dead-code path):

```
[agentweave-bridge] event: model.usage sessionKey: agent:main:main source: undefined
```

The downstream dashboard bucket that had been showing "unknown" for every codex turn now correctly attributes to `gpt-5.5`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Plugins subscribing via the public `onDiagnosticEvent` API never observe trusted `model.*` lifecycle events (`model.call.started/completed/error`, `model.usage`, `model.failover`) because the existing filter at `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts:879` drops every event whose dispatcher metadata is `trusted: true`. On my deployed install, this surfaced as Codex `gpt-5.5` turns bucketing as "unknown" in a downstream observability bridge plugin (agentweave-bridge) — the per-turn span never received `prov.llm.{provider,model}` because the bridge's `model.usage` / `model.call.completed` handlers were dead code against the trusted emit paths.
- Real environment tested: OpenClaw v2026.5.10-beta.1 gateway running under `systemctl --user` on Linux (Debian 12, Node 24.13 via nvm) on my NAS (192.168.1.70), driving a Codex subscription session via Telegram channel and the embedded pi-runner. Local install built from this PR head: `dist/` produced by `pnpm build` from commit 52f87ce58a, swapped into `/home/Arnab/clawd/projects/openclaw/dist/`, gateway restarted. Bridge plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/user-plugins/agentweave-bridge/`, rebuilt against the new SDK export.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```
  # 1. Build the patched openclaw from this branch
  cd /home/Arnab/dev/openclaw-model-usage
  CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  CI=true pnpm build

  # 2. Install over the canonical openclaw dist/
  systemctl --user stop openclaw-gateway
  mv /home/Arnab/clawd/projects/openclaw/dist /home/Arnab/clawd/projects/openclaw/dist.bak
  cp -r dist /home/Arnab/clawd/projects/openclaw/dist
  systemctl --user start openclaw-gateway

  # 3. Confirm trust-gated body in the built artifact
  grep -A2 "function onModelDiagnosticEvent" \
    /home/Arnab/clawd/projects/openclaw/dist/diagnostic-events-*.js

  # 4. Drive a real Codex turn through Telegram and observe the bridge plugin logs
  journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway -f | grep agentweave-bridge
  ```
- Evidence after fix:
  - Built-artifact contains the trust-gated callback:
    ```
    function onModelDiagnosticEvent(listener) {
      return onInternalDiagnosticEvent((event, metadata) => {
        if (!metadata.trusted) return;
    ```
  - Gateway startup logs from `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway` show the plugin subscribing to BOTH streams (previously only one):
    ```
    [agentweave-bridge] OTel SDK started, exporting to: http://192.168.1.70:30418/v1/traces
    [agentweave-bridge] subscribed to diagnostic events via plugin-sdk
    [agentweave-bridge] subscribed to model.* trusted events via plugin-sdk
    ```
  - During a real Telegram-initiated Codex turn (openai-codex/gpt-5.5), the bridge plugin now receives a trusted `model.usage` event that was previously invisible to it:
    ```
    [agentweave-bridge] started root span for main session: agent:main:main agent: nix-v1
    [agentweave-bridge] event: model.usage sessionKey: agent:main:main source: undefined
    [agentweave-bridge] ended root span for session: agent:main:main
    ```
- Observed result after fix: The downstream observability dashboard that had been bucketing every Codex turn as "unknown" model now correctly attributes them to `gpt-5.5`, with cost figures flowing through the bridge's pricing fallback. No behavior change for any other plugin: the broad `onDiagnosticEvent` subscription still filters every trusted event as before (defended by the regression test `onDiagnosticEvent still hides model.* trusted events from plugins`). A separate regression test confirms forged untrusted `model.*` events from `emitDiagnosticEvent` do NOT reach the new opt-in subscription.
- What was not tested: I did not exercise this against an isolated subagent (`agent:isolated:*`) session, only `agent:main:main`. Did not run on macOS or Windows; tested under Linux Node 24.13 only. Did not run the live `pnpm test` matrix exhaustively — the four review-required test files all pass locally (`src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts` 23/23, `src/plugins/contracts/plugin-sdk-index.test.ts` 5/5, `src/plugins/contracts/plugin-sdk-root-alias.test.ts` 13/13, `src/plugins/loader-sdk-import-guardrails.test.ts` 8/8) plus `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` and `pnpm build` are clean.

target.title: fix: route bindings return the wrong agent when route identifiers contain separators
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where routes that use distinct peer, guild, or role identifiers can return the wrong agent when an identifier contains a cache-key separator. The second route can reuse a cached result from a different routing context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route cache inputs are encoded as a structured JSON array so each field and role-array boundary remains distinct. The change preserves the existing order-insensitive role semantics while preventing delimiter-based collisions. This cache is process-local only: it is a `WeakMap` keyed by the active configuration object, so the change does not alter persisted state or require an upgrade migration.

## User Impact

Operators can safely route messages using identifiers that contain tabs, commas, or hyphens without another route's cached result being reused.

## Evidence

- Added regression coverage for peer/guild tab-delimiter collisions and role-ID comma-delimiter collisions.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/routing/resolve-route.test.ts` — 56 tests passed.

target.title: fix(sessions): read pinned session-extension registry in upstream monitor

## What Problem This Solves

`currentProviders()` in the session upstream-activity monitor read the **mutable** `getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry` to discover session-catalog providers. A standalone plugin load/reload swaps `activeRegistry` (via `setActivePluginRegistry` → `syncTrackedSurface(state.sessionExtension, …)`), so the long-lived background monitor could observe a post-swap registry with no catalogs and silently stop watching upstream activity.

This is the same drift class fixed upstream in `session-catalog.ts`, which now reads the bootstrap-pinned `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the pinned session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()?.sessionCatalogs`) instead of the mutable `activeRegistry`. The monitor is a persistent loop with no request-scoped pin, so it must use the stable surface the gateway already pins at startup.

## User Impact

The upstream-activity monitor keeps watching the correct session catalogs across plugin-registry churn instead of observing an empty set. No config or protocol change; no migration.

## Evidence

- Regression test `session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts` "reads the pinned session-extension registry after active registry churn": pins a registry carrying the provider, swaps the mutable `activeRegistry` to an empty one, asserts the monitor still calls the pinned provider. **Red before the fix** (`checkUpstreamActivity` called 0 times), green after.

- Verified `upstream/main` still reads the mutable `activeRegistry` (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The upstream monitor (`src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.ts`) read the session-extension catalog from the wrong registry state accessor (`getPluginRegistryState().activeRegistry`), which did not reflect the pinned/active session-extension registry. It now reads via `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()` so `currentProviders()` returns the live session catalogs used for upstream activity probing.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The fix is exercised by the existing test suite which drives the real session state database (`openOpenClawStateDatabase`) against throwaway temp dirs and asserts monitor tick behavior end to end.

target.title: fix(googlechat): media downloads can grow unbounded without a size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct callers of the Google Chat media download API could omit `maxBytes` and let a successful media response buffer through an uncapped `arrayBuffer()` call. The normal inbound attachment path already passes a configured cap, but the exported helper still had an uncapped fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat media downloads now use the existing 20 MiB Google Chat media default whenever callers do not provide a stricter cap. Existing callers that pass `maxBytes` keep their configured limit and the existing `Google Chat media exceeds max bytes (...)` error contract.

The fallback is fixed at the helper boundary because omitted `maxBytes` means the direct caller did not opt into a stricter call-specific cap. Normal inbound Google Chat attachment handling still passes the configured `mediaMaxMb` value explicitly.

## User Impact

Google Chat media downloads fail closed instead of risking unbounded memory growth from an oversized media response. Operators who lower `mediaMaxMb` or callers that pass a stricter `maxBytes` still get the stricter limit.

## Evidence

- Source proof on current `main`: `downloadGoogleChatMedia` can call `fetchBuffer` without `maxBytes`; `fetchBuffer` then falls back to `Response.arrayBuffer()` on successful responses.
- Local focused test: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts -- --run` -> 1 file / 26 tests passed.

target.title: fix(ui): bound managed image blob URL fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveManagedOutgoingImageBlobUrl` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.ts` fetches a managed chat image blob URL with `fetch(...)` **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled image endpoint hangs thumbnail resolution indefinitely.

Same unbounded-network-operation class as the many `fix(...)` "bound X" PRs: a request with no `AbortSignal` can block the caller forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the fetch in an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`MANAGED_IMAGE_BLOB_URL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`, alongside the existing `MANAGED_IMAGE_BLOB_URL_MISS_RETRY_MS`), following the Control UI convention. The timer is cleared in `finally`.

## User Impact

Chat image thumbnails fail fast instead of hanging when the image endpoint is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.ts` on `main` line 1552: `fetch(fetchUrl, { ... })` has no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into the request and clears the timeout.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Managed outgoing image blob resolution (`resolveManagedOutgoingImageBlobUrl` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.ts`) hangs forever when the gateway image endpoint never responds, because the `fetch(fetchUrl, { ... })` call has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24). The fix applies the same `AbortController` + `setTimeout(..., 30_000)` watchdog threaded into `fetch` as `signal`, cleared in `finally`, that PRs #110009 and #110010 already ship and prove with real local-HTTP-server tests (Nostr profile ops, chat avatar). #110009 / #110010 real-server tests: `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.test.ts` — both pass, showing a stalled endpoint aborts after the bound and a normal round trip still resolves.

- `node /Users/maomaoplanet/Projects/openclaw-evidence/pr-110011/repro.mjs`

Evidence after fix (standalone reproduction of the exact production fetch/signal/watchdog/clearTimeout pattern, using a 1s bound so it runs fast; production uses 30_000ms):
```
STALL  -> rejected: AbortError after 1004ms (bound 1000ms)
NORMAL -> resolved ok=true after 7ms
```

Observed result after fix: A stalled gateway endpoint is aborted via the `AbortController` watchdog (AbortError) instead of leaving the fetch pending forever; a responsive endpoint resolves normally. The production code path is identical to the already-proven #110009 / #110010 pattern, only the fetch target and 30s constant differ.

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750
Follow-up: #105877

## Current Status

The implementation and validation work is complete on the frozen final range:

```text
base: ee80377a22b36b1bff6faed20c9233134e2a186d
head: edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9
```

The branch intentionally stays on that reviewed and verified baseline. It will not continue chasing later `main` movement. GitHub currently reports the PR as `CONFLICTING / DIRTY` because `main` advanced again after the final rebase; that repository-level conflict is the only known landability blocker.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart could repeatedly select the same interrupted main session for automatic recovery. The existing retry loop was process-local, so supervisor backoff only delayed the next attempt: a session that never became healthy could be dispatched again after every restart without a durable ceiling.

This PR adds a durable, session-owned recovery fuse. The first three accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recovery attempts may dispatch. Before a fourth dispatch, OpenClaw persists an operator notice, tombstones the session, and requires recovery through inspection and `/new` or reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Recovery ownership

The durable state is the core-internal `InternalSessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` aggregate, separate from the public `SessionEntry` contract. It records the recovery cycle and revision, charged attempts, the exact pre-dispatch reservation, lifecycle-generation foreground claim tokens, and an optional terminal tombstone.

`src/agents/main-session-recovery-state.ts` owns the pure transitions. `src/agents/main-session-recovery-store.ts` owns atomic persistence against the canonical SQLite row. Gateway and direct agent-command ingress use the same identity, revision, reservation, lifecycle-generation, and foreground-owner rules.

The policy is:

- persist the charge and reservation before dispatch;
- roll back only when the exact request is known not to have been accepted;
- retain the charge when acceptance is uncertain, including a stale reservation after restart;
- allow three charged attempts, then persist the notice and tombstone before a fourth dispatch;
- do not reset the budget merely because time passes; and
- clear it after healthy non-aborted settlement, session replacement, or reset.

`restartRecoveryRuns` remains a lifecycle-generation fence rather than the durable retry budget. Subagent orphan recovery remains independently owned and retains its existing policy.

### Concurrency and restart safety

The final implementation includes:

- lifecycle-generation fences so stale cleanup cannot erase new work;
- Gateway recovery leases bound to the exact recovery identity;
- snapshot revision and foreground-claim checks around concurrent admission;
- stale lifecycle-clear suppression after tombstoning;
- predecessor preclaims during freshness rollover;
- exact reservation rollback across session-key canonicalization; and
- transcript-only exhaustion notice persistence before tombstoning, with retry when notice persistence fails.

### Plugin SDK boundary

Recovery coordination remains internal and does not become a plugin contract.

- Public session reads project internal rows to `SessionEntry`.
- Modern patch/upsert APIs strip escaped private input and preserve internal recovery state.
- Deprecated `loadSessionStore` and `updateSessionStore` now also project public rows and reconcile public mutations while preserving private recovery state and deletion semantics.
- The public testing result excludes the internal recovery candidate.
- The generated Plugin SDK surface contains no recovery-internal concept, and no checksum-only baseline update hides a semantic change.

The broader shipped Plugin SDK testing-barrel question remains tracked separately in #105877.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three charged accepted or acceptance-uncertain attempts, OpenClaw persists the operator notice and quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch. Healthy progress, replacement, or reset restores the full budget; waiting alone does not.

Plugins continue to see the public session contract and cannot observe or accidentally overwrite the internal recovery state through either modern or deprecated session-store APIs.

## Evidence

Exact frozen range:

```text
ee80377a22b36b1bff6faed20c9233134e2a186d..edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9
```

- Focused final regression set: 227 tests passed (`14` recovery-state, `15` Gateway lifecycle, `198` agent tests).
- Broader restart-recovery suite: 86 passed.
- Agent-command suite: 112 passed.
- Core production and test `tsgo` lanes passed.
- Targeted and changed-file `oxfmt` / `oxlint` passed.
- LOC ratchet passed for all 53 changed production TypeScript files.
- Full changed-file gate passed against the frozen base, including core/extension types, lint, Plugin SDK surface/API/exports, and repository guards.
- Full local build passed on Node `24.15.0`.
- Mandatory default-Codex Auto Review covered the final change in six synthetic slices plus the final dirty follow-up; no accepted/actionable finding remains.
- Thread-aware GitHub inspection found no unresolved inline review threads; the current maintainer review decision is `APPROVED`.

Final end-to-end proof used a local Docker container, actual provider `local-container`, lease `cbx_9736f8111fa1`, Ubuntu 26.04:

- complete container build passed;
- a real Gateway started successfully;
- exhausted recovery ended with `status=failed`, `abortedLastRun=false`, and `chargedAttempts=3`;
- the transcript notice was persisted; and
- the tombstone was written before any fourth dispatch.

Exact-head GitHub automation has passed the dependency and security guards plus one real-behavior proof run. The standard full CI workflow did not dispatch for this fork-head update. Exact-merge-result CI cannot exist while GitHub reports the later-main conflict.

## Known Blocker

The code, tests, review findings, and exact-head behavior proof are complete. GitHub currently reports `mergeable=CONFLICTING` and `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` after `main` advanced again. Per the frozen-branch decision, this PR will not be rebased or merged with another moving `main` baseline.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google provider responses could include malformed inline audio or video base64 that Node would decode permissively instead of rejecting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google music, speech, video generation, and Realtime Live audio now share a strict base64 decoder before materializing provider-returned media. The Google-specific decoder accepts both standard base64 and Google ProtoJSON-valid base64url payloads before canonical validation, while inline video bytes reuse the existing generated-video byte cap before decode so oversized payloads fail before allocating the full buffer.

## User Impact

Users get a clear provider error for malformed Google media responses without rejecting valid base64url media that Google may return. Realtime Live malformed inline audio is routed through `onError` without emitting corrupt audio, and operators keep the existing video media cap behavior without permissive base64 decoding.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):** after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners, each spawn site attaches no-op `error` listeners on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` (`processes.ts`, `http.ts`), mirroring `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle/finalization.

**Real integration proof — executes the patched code outside Vitest over a real WebSocket bridge.** A standalone `tsx` harness imports and calls the real exported entry points — `startProcess()` → `runProcess()` (process-RPC owner) and `httpRequest({streamResponse:true})` → `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest()` (HTTP owner) — over a real `ws` bridge. Only the sandbox backend seam is stubbed; the `spawn`, stdout/stderr listeners, close lifecycle, JSON-RPC notifications, and ws bridge are all real. No `spawn` module mock, no Vitest.

target.title: fix: avoid false macOS gateway restart failures
target.body:
Closes #109941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users restarting an installed gateway could receive a definitive "service stayed stopped" failure while launchd was still inside its normal `KeepAlive` throttle window and about to retry the service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed daemon and update restart paths now carry the already-known launchd `KeepAlive` supervision fact into restart health evaluation. That fact disables only the stopped-and-free early exit for the managed macOS path; the existing bounded restart deadline remains in force, while Linux, Windows, unmanaged, unloaded, and recovery paths without active KeepAlive supervision retain their existing early-failure behavior.

## User Impact

Managed macOS gateway restarts can recover after launchd's throttle interval without being reported as failed prematurely. A gateway that never becomes healthy still fails at the normal bounded timeout.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/daemon-cli/restart-health-wait.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts` - 3 files and 91 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves the previous Linux stopped/free path still exits at 12.5 seconds, the Windows path remains unchanged, a launchd-supervised restart can become healthy at 13 seconds, and a launchd-supervised service that never recovers reaches the bounded timeout.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` passed for all eight changed files.
- Native macOS LaunchAgent behavior passed in [run 29582901448](https://github.com/DaigoSoup/openclaw/actions/runs/29582901448) on `macos-15`. A real installed user LaunchAgent used a wrapper that failed its first two KeepAlive relaunches: `gateway restart --json` recovered successfully in 51 seconds after launch attempts at epoch seconds `1784294494`, `1784294514`, and `1784294524` (20-second then 10-second gaps), well beyond the former early cutoff. With every relaunch forced to fail, the command returned nonzero in 96 seconds end to end and reported `Gateway restart timed out after 60s waiting for health checks`; it did not report `service stayed stopped`. The workflow then uninstalled the LaunchAgent successfully.
- `check:changed` remote delegation was blocked before execution: Blacksmith reported `not authenticated`, and direct AWS required a Crabbox broker login. Focused tests and static checks above passed; PR CI is expected to supply the remaining typecheck/guard coverage.
- Exact-head PR CI is fully green in [run 29584559723](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29584559723): build artifacts, production/test typechecks, lint, QA smoke profiles, focused and broad Node shards, dependency checks, SQLite/session guards, and `openclaw/ci-gate` all passed. This run used head `6bec143bb742863ae4806be13fe184eb2a128966`, whose tree is byte-identical to the reviewed implementation head; the extra commit only retriggered checks after contributor permissions could not rerun the earlier unrelated SQLite flake.
- Autoreview was attempted with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted`; both the change review and its benign smoke harness failed in the Codex engine before returning a structured verdict. No autoreview finding was returned, and this is not claimed as review-clean.

This contribution is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation, tests, and affected daemon/update call paths and understand the change.

target.title: improve: speed up native session loading from paired Macs
target.body:
Closes #109838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where opening the Control UI could take tens of seconds to show native Claude Code and Codex sessions when several paired Macs had large local session histories.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude discovery now overlaps local and paired-node work. The macOS node keeps a bounded, identity-validated metadata cache and runs Claude filesystem discovery on a serialized utility worker, so it does not block Codex or unrelated node commands. Cancellation propagates through queued and active catalog work. Codex continues to use the complete canonical App Server listing path; this change does not trade completeness for speed.

## User Impact

Native Claude Code and Codex sessions populate much faster after the first scan, while preserving session completeness, pagination, permission checks, and offline-node behavior.

Release-note context: speed up native Claude Code and Codex session loading from paired Macs.

## Evidence

- Multi-node baseline observation before rollout: combined catalog request took 43.98s.
- Exact Developer ID-signed macOS build on a paired Mac, after process restart: Claude returned 40 rows plus a cursor in 3.744s cold and 0.737s on repeat; canonical Codex returned 40 rows plus a cursor in 2.751s.
- Warm combined Gateway request returned both catalogs with 80 rows each in 2.425s. Twenty-three offline paired records did not block healthy results.
- Focused Anthropic catalog tests: 26/26 passed.
- Focused macOS catalog/runtime tests after the final lint refactor: 36/36 passed.
- Pinned SwiftLint and SwiftFormat against the final macOS source: zero violations and zero files requiring formatting.
- Changed-surface Testbox gate passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29585460641
- Final-head autoreview: no actionable findings, correctness confidence 0.92.
- Browser visual inspection was unavailable because the existing Chrome DevTools bridge rejected attachment. Gateway logs still confirmed real Control UI catalog requests; no UI markup or visual behavior changed.

target.title: fix(msteams): bound remote media saves with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams inbound remote media saves could hang indefinitely when an attachment response returned headers and then stalled mid-body. `saveResponseMedia` / `saveRemoteMedia` were called without `readIdleTimeoutMs` (and without a header timeout on the runtime path), so a chunk stall never failed closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the same media timeout policy already used by Mattermost/Zalo/Tlon: `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000` and `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000` through both the direct `saveResponseMedia` path and the runtime `saveRemoteMedia` path.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Teams attachment download body could hang inbound media persistence forever.

**After:** Attachment body reads fail closed after 30s of idle (and header waits after 120s on the guarded path), so the inbound turn can surface a media failure instead of hanging.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/remote-media.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/remote-media.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` → `saveResponseMedia` / `channel.media.saveRemoteMedia`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Teams remote media saves now forward header and body-idle timeouts on both media paths.

### Canonical reachability path

`downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` → `saveRemoteMediaDirect` → `saveResponseMedia({ readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`, and the non-direct path → `saveRemoteMedia({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`.

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `image/png` headers plus one body chunk and then never sends another chunk or ends the response. The production `saveResponseMedia` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-runtime` — the exact function the direct Teams save path passes `readIdleTimeoutMs` into) is driven against that live socket with a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` media store, Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server sends media headers + one chunk then stalls; drive the
# production Teams save path against it (idle budget 300ms):
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx scripts/proof-msteams-media-idle-timeout.mts

# Supplemental focused regression:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/attachments/remote-media.test.ts --reporter=dot
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production Teams save path against a live socket):

```text
  ok: stalled attachment save rejected (not hung) — elapsed=325ms
  ok: save terminated (bounded, not infinite) — elapsed=325ms
  ok: idle-timeout failure surfaced — Failed to fetch media from https://teams.example.com/att.png: Media download stalled: no data received for 300ms
  ok: unbounded attachment read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing attachment saved — {}

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled `image/png` socket, `saveResponseMedia` fails closed in ~325ms with `Media download stalled: no data received for 300ms` and releases the connection. The negative control — an unbounded `arrayBuffer()` on the same socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing attachment still saves.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real Microsoft Teams attachment host.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the Teams media save timeout wiring and caller-path proof output.

## Summary

- apply portable stdio and remote MCP declarations through OpenClaw's validated source-config writer
- preserve `${ENV_VAR}` references and credential-free OAuth intent without storing server configuration in provenance
- reuse exact existing declarations, distinguish Claw-created from independently owned config, and allow multiple Claws to share one exact server

## Contract

- dry-run shows each MCP command or URL before consent; apply rechecks source config and uses create-only writes

- provenance stores only agent, name, redacted digest, ownership class, and lifecycle status
- pending writes reconcile deterministically against source config; unreadable source config fails planning before any cleanup
- remove releases independently owned, shared, missing, failed, or operator-modified declarations and uses compare-before-unset for the final Claw-created declaration
- cron jobs are disabled before MCP, agent, package, and workspace cleanup so scheduled work cannot race teardown

target.title: fix(qqbot): resolve start() when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping the QQBot gateway during or immediately after startup could leave `GatewayConnection.start()` pending forever when the caller AbortSignal was already aborted. The previous lifecycle also continued connecting after an early abort, which could leave a socket created during shutdown outside cleanup ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

`start()` registered abort listeners after work had already begun without normalizing an already-fired signal. The fix makes abort handling idempotent at registration, skips connection work for pre-aborted starts, and checks lifecycle ownership after each asynchronous startup stage. A socket created after an in-flight abort is closed before it can be adopted. Risk is limited to the QQBot connection startup and shutdown path; no config or protocol surface changes.

## User Impact

QQBot channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown overlaps startup, and startup does not retain a WebSocket that finishes opening after its lifecycle owner has stopped.

## Evidence

**Live configured-account proof (redacted):**

```
credentialExchangeSucceeded: true
abortPhase: after start invocation
outcome: resolved
elapsedMs: 146
existingGatewayLeftRunning: true
```

This ran the exported `GatewayConnection` with the locally configured QQBot app ID and secret file, forced a fresh real QQ credential exchange, then aborted immediately after invoking `start()`. The patched lifecycle resolved in 146 ms after the real credential request and stopped before gateway URL/socket adoption. The already-running live Gateway was left online, and no messages were sent.

**Deterministic before proof on the original implementation:**

```
label: before-fix
timedOut: true
elapsedMs: 501
resolved: false
exit: 1
```

The same exported-class harness with a pre-aborted signal exceeded its 500 ms bound before the fix.

**Focused regression tests:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway-connection.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       9 passed (9)
```

Coverage now verifies both that a pre-aborted start performs no socket creation and that a socket returned after an in-flight abort is immediately closed.

**Additional checks:**

```
$ pnpm format extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway-connection.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway-connection.test.ts
Finished on 2 files

$ git diff --check
# clean
```

`pnpm check:changed` attempted to delegate its heavy lane to unavailable maintainer Testbox infrastructure and exited before running the remote check. Full type/lint/build gates are therefore left to GitHub Actions. A full active-service restart was not performed because it would disrupt the existing live channel.

AI-assisted: Codex and Cursor; proof runs executed on this machine.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): suppress fallback after route-matched message tool
target.body:
When heartbeat runs in message-tool-only mode, a successful generic message tool delivery can still be followed by duplicate free-text fallback narration in the same Telegram chat.

Fixes #84217

## Affected surface

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`
  - Adds route-matched message tool delivery evidence for heartbeat replies only after the generic message tool sent to the same provider/target/account route.
- `src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds internal reply-payload metadata for route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat-reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds a heartbeat-specific evidence reader.
- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`
  - Suppresses free-text fallback only when the reply carries route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts`
  - Leaves heartbeat payloads available for heartbeat-specific route evidence instead of dropping them via generic message-tool dedupe first.
- Tests:
  - `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.tool-response.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`

## Scope

This is a parameter/evidence threading fix. It does not add a config flag, does not change heartbeat scheduling, and does not touch Slack identity, commitment, or channel-specific private paths.

The important semantic boundary is that "generic message tool delivery evidence" is not the same as "has outbound reply content". This PR only marks heartbeat replies when existing message-tool target evidence matches the same delivery route via the existing `resolveMessagingToolPayloadDedupe` route matcher. Global `messagingToolSentTexts` without route targets is intentionally not enough.

After Vincent's thread-route follow-up, I found one extra current-head issue while refreshing proof: generic reply-payload dedupe could drop the matched heartbeat payload before `heartbeat-runner` saw the route evidence. The current head keeps heartbeat payloads out of that generic dedupe layer so the heartbeat-specific suppression path receives the evidence and can still preserve no-route / wrong-topic fallback behavior.

## Prior art

Prior attempt #84273 was closed by contributor due to inability to provide live channel proof. This PR provides expanded source + runtime helper proof, with the helper semantic explicitly distinguishing "generic message tool delivery evidence" from "has outbound reply content" to address the message-delivery risk flagged in #84273.

The key difference from #84273 is route scope: #84273 marked heartbeat payloads after any message-tool send, while this PR only marks a heartbeat payload when committed `messagingToolSentTargets` match the reply route. If the message tool delivered to another route, or only global text evidence exists, heartbeat fallback still sends.

## Current-head P1 follow-up proof

This update addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Suppress same-route fallback even when the text differs" on head `25958135ed2135dede29e716668ac34cfaea8007`.

The same-route heartbeat evidence rule now treats committed route-matched generic `message` tool target evidence as sufficient for a single plain heartbeat fallback payload, even when the fallback text differs from the tool body. Multi-payload heartbeat replies keep the existing text-match guard so unrelated fallback payloads are not suppressed. Rich payloads, media payloads, reasoning, no-route evidence, wrong-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic evidence remain outside this suppression path.

## Current-head maintenance proof

After Vincent's route/thread follow-up moved this PR to `f21343bfd4`, CI exposed one current-head regression: `checks-node-auto-reply-reply-agent-runner` timed out in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts` at `dedupes duplicate same-target reply text without suppressing unrelated finals`.

Root cause: route dedupe called `getChannelPlugin("telegram")` from the generic reply-payload path, which lazily loads the bundled Telegram plugin in this test/runtime path and can block the shard. ## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** heartbeat message-tool-only delivery should not send duplicate free-text fallback after the generic `message` tool has already delivered to the same route, but it must still send fallback when no same-route delivery evidence exists.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw checkout on Linux, Node 22.22.2, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `wolf/heartbeat-suppress-after-message-tool`, head `14b8854108`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ran a local OpenClaw runtime helper that imports production `runHeartbeatOnce`, seeds a real `openclaw.json`-shaped config and session store, registers a local Telegram outbound adapter, then executes three heartbeat ticks: same-route evidence, no-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic-unmarked evidence.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the runtime helper:

- **Observed result after fix:** with route-scoped message-tool evidence, `runHeartbeatOnce` completes and does not invoke the Telegram send path (`telegramSendCount: 0`), so the fallback narration is suppressed. Without route evidence, and for the wrong-topic/wrong-thread-unmarked fallback case, the same runtime path invokes the Telegram send path once (`telegramSendCount: 1`), proving fallback remains available when the message tool did not prove same-route delivery.
- **What was not tested:** I did not run a live Telegram heartbeat tick with a real bot token/chat. I did not test Slack/WhatsApp live channels; the patch is heartbeat reply evidence and generic runner fallback suppression, with Telegram-shaped runtime coverage for the reported duplicate free-text path.

- `handles approval IDs with emoji without crashing`: Verifies sliceUtf16Safe is exercised by passing an emoji-containing approval ID (with surrogate pair at 8-char boundary) through handleRequested and handleResolved. Confirms the forwarder does not crash and produces a non-empty approval slug.
- `produces valid approval slugs for normal IDs`: Verifies that normal approval IDs produce the expected 8-character slug via sliceUtf16Safe.

---

### Real behavior proof (Unicode safety demonstration)

A live demo script was run to compare the old behavior (`String.prototype.slice(0, 8)`) vs the new behavior (`sliceUtf16Safe(id, 0, 8)`) across various Unicode approval IDs:

```
(sliceUtf16Safe(id, 0, 8)) for truncated approval slugs.

shown to users in the channel to identify which approval to
respond to (approve/deny). If the boundary splits an emoji,
users see a broken character and may not recognize the ID.

  NEW (sliceUtf16Safe):     "123456😀"
```

| `1234567👨` (len=9) | `1234567�` — broken surrogate | `1234567` — backtracked |

All affected tests pass (25 tests across 2 test files):

target.title: fix(ci): bound release-checks git fetch operations with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the openclaw-release-checks workflow could remain stuck in either of its two `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks release validation checks and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `git fetch "$@"` commands (L227 and L288) now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All release-check logic and non-network operations are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing a release-checks runner for the full job timeout before validation begins.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts --run --testNamePattern="bounds release-checks git fetch"` ??1 passed.

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each production workflow step, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a Git transport that stalls until `TERM`. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds, the Git fixture observed `TERM`, and none reached the five-second outer watchdog.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete test suite was also attempted: all tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases were skipped. The affected focused regression is green.

target.title: fix(openai): bound stalled generated video download body reads with idle timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI generated-video downloads call `readResponseWithLimit()` with a `maxBytes` cap but without `chunkTimeoutMs`. A CDN that accepts the connection and then stops sending body chunks can leave the download Promise pending indefinitely, holding Gateway connection capacity under concurrent video downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` on the OpenAI video download reader, matching the landed DashScope / Google pattern. Re-resolve the remaining operation budget after headers arrive and fail closed when that budget is exhausted — never revive a fresh `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. Teach the shared provider-HTTP test mock to use absolute `deadlineAtMs` so remaining budget decays like production. Add a caller-path `generateVideo` regression that feeds a never-chunking body.

Sibling providers (BytePlus, Runway, Together, fal, OpenRouter, MiniMax) are intentionally out of scope for this PR and will follow as separately proven one-provider PRs.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled OpenAI generated-video download body could hang the provider download forever.

**After:** The download body read fails closed after the remaining operation idle budget with `OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for Nms`, then releases the connection.

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts` | Remaining-budget resolver + `chunkTimeoutMs` / `onIdleTimeout` on download body read |
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts` | Caller-path stalled-body regression |
| `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/provider-http-mocks.ts` | Deadline mock uses `deadlineAtMs` and decaying remaining budget |

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled OpenAI generated-video download bodies now fail closed on the remaining operation idle budget instead of hanging forever.

### Canonical reachability path

`generateVideo` → `downloadOpenAIVideo` → `readResponseWithLimit(response, maxBytes, { chunkTimeoutMs, onIdleTimeout })` (`extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts`)

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `video/mp4` headers plus one body chunk and then never sends another chunk or ends the response. The production shared reader (`readResponseWithLimit` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` — the exact runtime the download path imports) is driven against that live socket with the OpenAI download option bag. Node v22+.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server sends video/mp4 headers + one chunk then stalls; drive the
# production download reader against it (idle budget 300ms):
node --import tsx scripts/proof-video-gen-idle-timeout.mts

# Supplemental caller-path regression through generateVideo:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production reader against a live video socket):

```text
  ok: stalled video download rejected (not hung) — elapsed=322ms
  ok: download idle-timeout error surfaced — OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 300ms
  ok: terminated within ~idle budget — elapsed=322ms
  ok: unbounded video body read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing video body read intact — bytes=7

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

Supplemental caller-path regression (`generateVideo` → stalled download):

```text
 ✓ openai video generation provider > times out stalled generated video download bodies via chunkTimeoutMs 81ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled `video/mp4` socket, the production download reader rejects in ~322ms with `OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 300ms` and releases the connection. The negative control — an unbounded `arrayBuffer()` on the same socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing body still reads intact. The caller-path `generateVideo` regression rejects in 81ms under an 80ms deadline (not the 120s default).

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real OpenAI Sora CDN endpoint. Sibling providers are deferred to follow-up PRs.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the remaining-budget resolver against DashScope, the decaying mock deadline contract, and caller-path plus loopback proof output.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md Ticket: [Bug: Skill Workshop Apply overwrites SKILL.md with proposal text verbatim (data loss)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107707).

Codex review identified two P1 issues in the initial patch:
1. **Write-before-guard**: `applySkillProposal` computed `requiresExplicitApproval` but called `writeWorkspaceSkill` before returning the flag, so any shared-service caller (CLI, Gateway) could overwrite content without presenting an approval grant.
2. **Missing metadata validation**: `parseFrontmatter` only checked parse success; `name` and `description` fields were not verified before overwriting SKILL.md.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (missing `name` or `description`) are hard-rejected before any write
- Low-continuity update proposals are **blocked at the shared service boundary** — SKILL.md is never written unless the caller presents an explicit approval grant (`explicitApprovalGranted=true` via `--approve` flag, Gateway approval dialog, or agent tool after policy hook approval)
- Substantially continuous updates (≥3 shared non-heading lines, ≥50% original content retained) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- CLI `skills workshop apply` gains `--approve` flag (default false) for manual low-continuity override
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies
- Bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) shown in approval descriptions and apply results

**Maintainer decision needed**: The low-continuity approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for low-continuity updates while substantially continuous updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `d978145d757d`**

### P1 #1: Block low-continuity writes in the apply service

Codex review finding: `validateApplyBody only records requiresExplicitApproval; applySkillProposal then writes the replacement and returns the flag afterward. Make the service stop before writeWorkspaceSkill unless the caller supplies authoritative explicit approval for a low-continuity replacement.` (confidence 0.99 → resolved ✅)

Fix at `src/skills/workshop/service.ts:601-605`:

```typescript
if (bodyValidation.requiresExplicitApproval && !input.explicitApprovalGranted) {
  throw new Error("Update requires explicit approval...");
}
await writeWorkspaceSkill({ ... });
```

Callers: agent tool + Gateway pass `explicitApprovalGranted: true`, CLI defaults to `explicitApprovalGranted: false` (requires `--approve`).

### P1 #2: Validate required SKILL.md frontmatter fields

Codex review finding: `parseFrontmatter(skillContent) proves only that the frontmatter can be parsed; this code never checks that name and description are present and non-empty before overwriting the target.` (confidence 0.97)

Fix at `src/skills/workshop/service.ts:664-675`:

```typescript
const name = parsed["name"];
const description = parsed["description"];
if (!name || name.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error("...name..."); }
if (!description || description.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error("...description..."); }
```

### Live real behavior proof (exact head SHA `d978145d757d`)

All 12 scenarios pass on the current head:

```console
=== Comprehensive Real Behavior Proof ===
SHA: d978145d757d
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T13:57:43.484Z
Node: v24.13.1

=== SECTION 1: Service Boundary Guard ===
1a CLI no --approve: Update requires explicit approval; proposal has
  insufficient content continuity with the current skill.
1a SKILL.md unchanged: true
1b CLI with --approve: written=true, contains "New A.": true

=== SECTION 2: Approval Hook ===
2a low-continuity: requireApproval (BLOCKED), file unchanged: true
2b high-continuity: undefined (ALLOWED)

=== SECTION 3: Incidental Overlap ===
3a heading-only: BLOCKED
3b 1-line overlap: BLOCKED
3c 2-line overlap: BLOCKED
3d substantial (4/6, 67%): requiresExplicitApproval=false

=== SECTION 4: Frontmatter Validation ===
4a missing name: guard blocks
4b missing description: guard blocks
4c empty body: "Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter"

=== SECTION 5: Change Summary ===
changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines

=== Summary ===
1. Service guard blocks write before writeWorkspaceSkill
2. Approval hook blocks low-continuity, allows high-continuity
3. Incidental heading-only/1-line/2-line overlap: all BLOCKED
4. Substantial continuity (4/6, 67%): allowed
5. Missing name/description: hard rejection before write
6. Empty body: hard rejection
7. Change summary recorded
```

Note for Section 4a/4b: `proposeUpdateSkill` always generates proposal frontmatter with `name` and `description`, so the name/description check in `validateApplyBody` is a defense-in-depth guard. The protection path is: service boundary guard → (on explicit approval) → validateApplyBody re-checks frontmatter fields → write.

### Unit tests (exact head SHA `d978145d757d`)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts \
    src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts \
    src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts \
    --run

 ✓ apply-body-validation.test.ts (4 tests)
 ✓ policy.test.ts (9 tests)
 ✓ service.test.ts (35 tests)

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  48 passed (48)
```

### Code review findings status

| Finding | File | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| [P1] Block low-continuity writes in the apply service | `service.ts:601-605` | ✅ Guard before `writeWorkspaceSkill` |
| [P1] Validate required SKILL.md frontmatter fields | `service.ts:664-675` | ✅ `name`, `description` non-empty |
| [P2] Remove machine-local iCodeMate configuration | `.icodemate/skills.json` | ✅ Already removed from branch |
| [P1] Maintainer decision: approval-policy owner confirmation | — | ⏳ Requires shakkernerd |

**Pre-existing CI issues**: `startup-memory` RSS 425 MB limit and `test/install-sh-docker.test.ts` format — both from `main`, not this PR.
